title: Learning to Generate Reviews and Discovering Sentiment
summary: A byte-level multiplicative LSTM language model trained on 82M Amazon reviews learns representations containing a disentangled 'sentiment unit'; a linear classifier on these features achieves state-of-the-art binary SST accuracy, and clamping the unit steers generation sentiment (paper Sections 1-4).

title: Real-Time User-Guided Image Colorization with Learned Deep Priors
summary: A CNN (per Section 3.4 / Fig. 2) that maps a grayscale Lab-L image plus sparse user color points (or global histogram/saturation hints) to ab color channels in a single feed-forward pass, trained on 1.3M ImageNet images with simulated user inputs using a smooth-L1 loss, plus a side branch predicting per-pixel color distributions for palette recommendations.

title: Proceedings of Workshop AEW10: Concepts in Information Theory and Communications
summary: This is a workshop proceedings collection (information theory and communications), not a neural network architecture paper. The only machine-learning contribution with implementable detail is Imanishi & Wadayama's binarized autoencoder for lossy compression feeding a pattern classifier (MNIST), trained with cross-entropy loss. No conversational model is described anywhere in the paper.

title: Recalibrating Fully Convolutional Networks with Spatial and Channel 'Squeeze & Excitation' Blocks
summary: The paper (Sections I-II) proposes three recalibration blocks for F-CNN segmentation: cSE (spatial squeeze via global average pooling, channel excitation via bottleneck FC layers), sSE (channel squeeze via 1x1 convolution, spatial excitation), and scSE (combined via max-out/add/mul/concat aggregation), placed after encoder and decoder blocks (P5), yielding Dice gains of ~4-9% with ~1.5% parameter increase.

title: GAN Lab: Understanding Complex Deep Generative Models using Interactive Visual Experimentation
summary: The paper presents GAN Lab, a browser-based interactive visualization tool (built on TensorFlow.js) that lets non-experts train small GANs on 2D toy datasets and inspect the generator/discriminator interplay via a model overview graph, layered distributions view, metrics (KL/JS divergence), and step-by-step training controls. It is a human-computer interaction/visualization contribution, not a new model architecture.

title: MeshCNN: A Network with an Edge
summary: MeshCNN is a CNN operating directly on triangular meshes: edges are the basic units, convolution uses the four edges incident to the two adjacent triangles with symmetric functions for order invariance, and pooling is a learned, task-driven edge-collapse that reduces the mesh while preserving topology (Sections 1, 3, 4).

title: Rethinking the Value of Network Pruning
summary: Empirically shows that for structured pruning, training the pruned (small) target architecture from scratch matches or beats the train-prune-fine-tune pipeline, implying pruning is valuable mainly as implicit architecture search rather than weight selection.

title: Wizard of Wikipedia: Knowledge-Powered Conversational agents
summary: The paper introduces the Wizard of Wikipedia dataset (grounded open-domain dialogues with Wikipedia knowledge) and Transformer Memory Network architectures that retrieve, attend over, and condition on knowledge to produce retrieval or generative dialogue responses (Sections 1, 3, 4).

title: CCNet: Criss-Cross Attention for Semantic Segmentation
summary: Proposes criss-cross attention that aggregates context along each pixel's row and column, applied recurrently (RCCA, R=2) so every pixel gathers full-image context at O(N√N) cost instead of O(N²), plus a category consistent loss for more discriminative features; achieves state-of-the-art segmentation results on Cityscapes, ADE20K, LIP, CamVid and COCO.

title: Bag of Freebies for Training Object Detection Neural Networks
summary: The paper surveys training-time tweaks (visually coherent mixup for detection, label smoothing, cosine LR schedule with warmup, synchronized BatchNorm, random shape training, data augmentation) that improve YOLOv3 and Faster R-CNN accuracy on Pascal VOC and COCO without changing architectures or inference cost (Sections 3-4).

title: Neural MMO: A Massively Multiagent Game Environment for Training and Evaluating Intelligent Agents
summary: The paper introduces a persistent, massively multiagent RL environment (a 'Neural MMO') with procedural tile-based maps, foraging and combat systems, and shows that larger agent populations magnify exploration and that unshared-weight populations diverge into behavioral niches (per Sections 3-5).

title: SciBERT: A Pretrained Language Model for Scientific Text
summary: A BERT-based language model pretrained on 3.17B tokens of scientific text (Semantic Scholar corpus) with a new in-domain WordPiece vocabulary (SciVocab), improving performance on scientific NLP tasks over BERT-Base.

title: Feature Generation by Convolutional Neural Network for Click-Through Rate Prediction
summary: FGCNN augments CTR feature spaces automatically: a CNN+pooling+recombination (fully connected) stack generates new interaction features from field embeddings, which are concatenated with raw embeddings and classified by an IPNN-style deep classifier, outperforming nine baselines on three datasets.

title: Text Classification Algorithms: A Survey
summary: A survey (not a novel model) describing the text-classification pipeline: feature extraction (TF-IDF, word embeddings), dimensionality reduction (PCA, LDA, NMF, random projection, autoencoders, t-SNE), classifiers (Rocchio, boosting/bagging, LR, Naive Bayes, KNN, SVM, decision trees, random forest, CRF, and deep learning: DNN, RNN/LSTM/GRU, CNN, DBN, HAN, RMDL, HDLTex), and evaluation metrics (accuracy, F-beta, MCC, ROC/AUC).

title: PIFu: Pixel-Aligned Implicit Function for High-Resolution Clothed Human Digitization
summary: PIFu is a pixel-aligned implicit representation that pairs a fully convolutional image encoder with MLP-based implicit functions to reconstruct high-resolution 3D geometry and texture of clothed humans from a single image, extendable to multiple views (paraphrased from Sections 1 and 3).

title: BERT Rediscovers the Classical NLP Pipeline
summary: The paper probes frozen BERT encoders with edge-probing classifiers and finds that linguistic information (POS, constituents, dependencies, entities, SRL, coreference) is encoded in layer orderings matching the classical NLP pipeline, using scalar mixing weights and cumulative layer-wise scoring.

title: Gradio: Hassle-Free Sharing and Testing of ML Models in the Wild
summary: A Python library (Gradio) that wraps trained ML models in shareable web interfaces so domain experts can interact with, manipulate inputs on, and flag errors from models without code (Sections 1, 3).

title: Detecting Photoshopped Faces by Scripting Photoshop
summary: The paper trains CNNs entirely on automatically generated fake data (Photoshop Face-Aware Liquify warps scripted on real face photos) to (1) classify whether a face image has been warped and (2) predict the per-pixel optical-flow warp field so the manipulation can be localized and partially undone.

title: MediaPipe: A Framework for Building Perception Pipelines
summary: MediaPipe is a framework (not a model) for building perception applications as directed graphs of reusable 'calculator' components connected by timestamped data streams, with scheduling, synchronization, GPU support, and performance tooling. It describes no neural network architecture, training procedure, or benchmark results that Zerfoo could reproduce as a numeric classifier.

title: Neural Machine Translation with Byte-Level Subwords
summary: Proposes byte-level BPE (BBPE) vocabularies for NMT: UTF-8 bytes as base symbols, showing comparable quality to character BPE with ~1/8 vocabulary size, better multilingual sharing, no OOV tokens enabling cross-script transfer, and demonstrating that contextualizing BBPE embeddings (depth-wise conv or bi-GRU) is necessary.

title: ABSApp: A Portable Weakly-Supervised Aspect-Based Sentiment Extraction System
summary: A weakly-supervised ABSA system that bootstraps domain-specific aspect/opinion lexicons from unlabeled text, lets users edit lexicons (~15 min), then classifies aspect-opinion sentiment pairs; no labeled training data required (paraphrase of Sections 1-3).

title: HuggingFace's Transformers: State-of-the-art Natural Language Processing
summary: A technical report describing the Transformers open-source library: a unified API of tokenizer + Transformer + task head, a community model hub for pretrained checkpoints, and deployment paths (TorchScript, ONNX, CoreML). It is a library/system paper, not a single model paper.

title: ClusterFit: Improving Generalization of Visual Representations
summary: ClusterFit is a post-hoc representation-improvement procedure: features from a pre-trained network are k-means clustered, and a new network is trained from scratch on cluster assignments as pseudo-labels, yielding more transferable visual features (paraphrase of Sections 1, 3.1).

title: Detection and Tracking Meet Drones Challenge
summary: This paper (Sections 1, 3, 8) presents the VisDrone benchmark — a large-scale drone-captured dataset with 263 video clips (179,264 frames) and 10,209 static images, over 2.5 million annotated bounding boxes in 10 categories — and summarizes four challenge tracks (image detection DET, video detection VID, single-object tracking SOT, multi-object tracking MOT) held with ECCV 2018–2020, reviewing submitted methods and future directions. It is a benc

title: PolyGen: An Autoregressive Generative Model of 3D Meshes
summary: PolyGen (per Sections 1-2) autoregressively models 3D polygon meshes directly: a Transformer-decoder vertex model over 8-bit quantized (z,y,x) coordinate sequences, and a Transformer-based face model using pointer networks over vertex indices, with optional class/image/voxel conditioning.

title: MNN: A Universal and Efficient Inference Engine
summary: MNN is a mobile inference engine (not a trainable model) whose contributions are a pre-inference runtime optimization mechanism (cost-based scheme selection and preparation-execution decoupling), kernel optimizations (Winograd convolution, Strassen matrix multiplication, NC4HW4 layout), and a backend abstraction enabling hybrid CPU/GPU scheduling with a lightweight binary footprint.

title: Pre-trained Models for Natural Language Processing: A Survey
summary: A survey (not a single model paper) that taxonomizes pre-trained language models by representation type, architecture, pre-training task, and extensions, and reviews adaptation methods such as fine-tuning, adapters, prompting, and compression.

title: 3D Photography using Context-aware Layered Depth Inpainting
summary: Converts a single RGB-D image into a layered depth image (LDI) with explicit pixel connectivity, iteratively inpainting color, depth, and depth edges at disocclusions using context-aware CNNs, enabling photorealistic novel view synthesis rendered as a textured mesh.

title: CNN Explainer: Learning Convolutional Neural Networks with Interactive Visualization
summary: An interactive web-based visualization tool (CNN Explainer) that teaches beginners how a small pre-trained CNN (Tiny VGG) classifies images, via an Overview, Elastic Explanation Views, and Interactive Formula Views. The paper is a HCI/visualization contribution, not a new model architecture.

title: Consistent Video Depth Estimation
summary: A test-time fine-tuning method that adapts a pre-trained single-image depth network per video using geometric consistency losses (spatial and disparity) derived from COLMAP camera poses and optical-flow correspondences, yielding dense, temporally consistent, geometrically consistent depth from casually captured monocular video.

title: PyTorch Distributed: Experiences on Accelerating Data Parallel Training
summary: A systems paper describing the design, implementation, and evaluation of PyTorch v1.5 DistributedDataParallel (DDP): gradient bucketing, overlapping AllReduce communication with backward computation, skipping gradient synchronizations (no_sync), and round-robin process groups, achieving near-linear scaling on 256 GPUs. It is not a model architecture paper.

title: Pay Attention when Required
summary: The paper uses differentiable neural architecture search over Transformer-XL layers (choosing self-attention, feed-forward, or identity per layer) and derives two design rules: self-attention is only needed in the former two-thirds of layers, and a layers-to-attention ratio of p:1 (p=5) suffices. The resulting PAR Transformer replaces ~63% of attention blocks with feed-forward blocks, retaining perplexity while cutting latency ~35% (Sections 2-3)

title: TODS: An Automated Time Series Outlier Detection System
summary: TODS is a modular AutoML system for time series outlier detection built from 70 'primitives' (functions with hyperparameters) across data processing, time series processing, feature analysis, detection algorithms, and a reinforcement module; pipelines are DAGs, constructed via GUI or a data-driven searcher (per 'TODS System' section).

title: Hypersim: A Photorealistic Synthetic Dataset for Holistic Indoor Scene Understanding
summary: The paper introduces Hypersim, a photorealistic synthetic dataset of 77,400 images from 461 indoor scenes with per-pixel instance segmentation, geometry, and a disentangled lighting decomposition (diffuse reflectance, diffuse illumination, non-diffuse residual), plus a generation pipeline and annotation tool. It demonstrates sim-to-real transfer for semantic segmentation (NYUv2) and 3D shape prediction (Pix3D). It is a dataset paper, not a model-

title: FLERT: Document-Level Features for Named Entity Recognition
summary: The paper evaluates document-level context (64 subtokens of left/right context per sentence) for NER in two architectures (fine-tuned Transformer-Linear and feature-based LSTM-CRF), finding document features improve F1 and fine-tuning outperforms feature-based approaches, with new state-of-the-art results on CoNLL-03 datasets (Sections 1-4).

title: Differentiable Data Augmentation with Kornia
summary: A review of Kornia's differentiable data augmentation (DDA) module: augmentation layers placed inside the computation graph so gradients flow through image transformations, plus benchmarks against TorchVision/Albumentations and use-cases (learned local feature orientation estimation, optimizable augmentation policies).

title: Continuous Surface Embeddings
summary: The paper (CSE, Novotny et al., NeurIPS 2020) replaces DensePose's manually charted UV representation with learnable per-vertex embedding vectors on a canonical mesh, expressed in a Laplace-Beltrami operator (LBO) spectral basis, and uses functional maps to transfer a single dense-pose predictor across object categories (humans to animals).

title: torchdistill: A Modular, Configuration-Driven Framework for Knowledge Distillation
summary: The paper presents torchdistill, a PyTorch-based open-source framework for knowledge distillation studies that uses declarative PyYAML configurations, module abstractions, a registry, forward-hook-based intermediate-output extraction, teacher-output caching, model redesigning, and stage-wise training; it reimplements many distillation methods and reproduces ImageNet and COCO results (Sections 2-3).

title: Nerfies: Deformable Neural Radiance Fields
summary: Extends NeRF with a per-image latent-conditioned SE(3) deformation field, elastic regularization of the deformation Jacobian's singular values, background regularization, and coarse-to-fine annealed positional encoding, enabling photorealistic free-viewpoint reconstruction of non-rigid scenes from casual monocular phone captures (per Sections 1, 3, 5).

title: pixelNeRF: Neural Radiance Fields from One or Few Images
summary: A learning framework that predicts a NeRF-style radiance field conditioned on one or few posed images via a fully convolutional pixel-aligned image encoder, trained across scenes with only 2D reconstruction (volume rendering) supervision, enabling feed-forward novel view synthesis without per-scene test-time optimization (paraphrase of Sections 1, 4).

title: MLS: A Large-Scale Multilingual Dataset for Speech Research
summary: Introduces Multilingual LibriSpeech (MLS), a public-domain read-speech corpus of ~50K hours across 8 languages built from LibriVox audiobooks via pseudo-labeling and transcript retrieval, plus released language models and baseline ASR results (paper Sections 1, 3-6).

title: ERNIE-M: Enhanced Multilingual Representation by Aligning Cross-lingual Semantics with Monolingual Corpora
summary: ERNIE-M is a cross-lingual pre-training method (built on XLM-R) that combines masked language modeling with two new objectives: cross-attention masked language modeling (CAMLM) on parallel corpora and back-translation masked language modeling (BTMLM), which generates pseudo-parallel tokens from monolingual text so cross-lingual semantic alignment can be learned without large parallel corpora.

title: Towards Real-World Blind Face Restoration with Generative Facial Prior
summary: GFP-GAN performs blind face restoration in a single forward pass by using a pretrained face GAN (StyleGAN2) as a generative facial prior, connected to a U-Net degradation removal module via latent code mapping and Channel-Split Spatial Feature Transform (CS-SFT) layers, with component and identity losses.

title: Neural Volume Rendering: NeRF And Beyond
summary: An annotated bibliography surveying the 2020 'NeRF explosion': precursor implicit-surface methods (Occupancy Networks, DeepSDF), the NeRF method itself, and follow-up work grouped by performance, dynamic scenes, relighting, shape, composition, and pose estimation. It proposes no new method, architecture, training procedure, or experimental results.

title: ViLT: Vision-and-Language Transformer Without Convolution or Region Supervision
summary: ViLT replaces heavy convolutional/region-based visual embedders in VLP models with a simple linear patch projection, feeding image and text tokens through a single-stream transformer (initialized from ViT-B/32) and pre-training with ITM, WPA, and MLM objectives, achieving competitive downstream performance at a fraction of the runtime (paper Sections 1-3).

title: LightSpeech: Lightweight and Fast Text to Speech with Neural Architecture Search
summary: LightSpeech applies neural architecture search (GBDT-NAS) over a chain-structured search space of lightweight operations (MHSA variants, depthwise-separable convolutions, FFN) for the FastSpeech 2 encoder/decoder, yielding a 1.8M-parameter TTS model with 15x compression, 16x fewer MACs, and 6.5x CPU speedup at on-par voice quality (paper-reported).

title: CodeXGLUE: A Machine Learning Benchmark Dataset for Code Understanding and Generation
summary: CodeXGLUE is a benchmark of 14 datasets across 10 program understanding/generation tasks, with three baseline systems (CodeBERT, CodeGPT, Encoder-Decoder) and an evaluation platform. It is a benchmark paper, not a single novel architecture.

title: End-to-end Audio-visual Speech Recognition with Conformers
summary: A hybrid CTC/attention AVSR model that learns features end-to-end from raw audio waveforms (1D-ResNet-18) and raw pixels (3D-conv + ResNet-18), fuses them via an MLP, and uses Conformer encoders plus a transformer decoder, achieving state-of-the-art WER on LRS2/LRS3 (per Sections 3-5).

title: Revisiting ResNets: Improved Training and Scaling Strategies
summary: The paper disentangles architecture, training, and scaling for ResNets, showing improved training methods (cosine LR decay, RandAugment, label smoothing, dropout, stochastic depth, EMA, reduced weight decay) plus ResNet-D and Squeeze-and-Excitation changes and new scaling strategies (depth scaling when overfitting; slow image-resolution scaling) yield ResNet-RS models matching EfficientNets at 1.7x-2.7x TPU speedup.

title: OGB-LSC: A Large-Scale Challenge for Machine Learning on Graphs
summary: The paper introduces OGB-LSC, three very large graph datasets (MAG240M node classification, WikiKG90M knowledge-graph completion, PCQM4M molecular graph regression), with baseline experiments showing expressive graph models outperform simple scalable ones, plus KDD Cup 2021 winning techniques and post-competition dataset updates.

title: FastMoE: A Fast Mixture-of-Expert Training System
summary: FastMoE is a PyTorch-based distributed Mixture-of-Experts training system for GPUs, providing flexible MoE layers (gate + top-k expert selection), optimized batched FFN expert computation, and expert-parallel placement across GPUs/nodes (paper Sections 1, 3).

title: speechocean762: An Open-Source Non-native English Speech Corpus For Pronunciation Assessment
summary: The paper introduces speechocean762, an open-source corpus of 5000 English utterances from 250 Mandarin-speaking non-native speakers (half children), annotated by five experts at sentence, word, and phoneme levels, plus a Kaldi baseline recipe using the NN-based GOP method with per-phone regressors (SVR / polynomial regression) for phoneme-level scoring (paper Sections 1-4).

title: Timers and Such: A Practical Benchmark for Spoken Language Understanding with Numbers
summary: Introduces Timers and Such, an open CC0-licensed dataset of spoken English commands involving numbers (SetTimer, SetAlarm, SimpleMath, UnitConversion intents), with real and VoiceLoop-synthesized audio, plus decoupled, multistage, and direct end-to-end SLU baselines in SpeechBrain (paper Sections 1-2, 5).

title: Image Super-Resolution via Iterative Refinement
summary: SR3 adapts denoising diffusion probabilistic models to conditional image generation, performing super-resolution by iteratively denoising pure Gaussian noise with a U-Net conditioned on the upsampled low-resolution image, achieving near-50% human fool rate on 8x face super-resolution and enabling cascaded high-resolution generation.

title: FreshDiskANN: A Fast and Accurate Graph-Based ANN Index for Streaming Similarity Search
summary: The paper introduces FreshVamana, a graph-based approximate nearest neighbor (ANN) index with update rules (alpha-RNG-preserving insert/delete) that keep recall stable under streaming insertions and deletions, and FreshDiskANN, a system combining an SSD-resident long-term index with in-memory temporary indices consolidated via a write-efficient StreamingMerge procedure (Sections 1.2, 4, 5).

title: CogView: Mastering Text-to-Image Generation via Transformers
summary: CogView is a 4-billion-parameter autoregressive GPT-style Transformer trained on 30M Chinese text-image pairs with a VQ-VAE image tokenizer for general-domain text-to-image generation, plus stabilization techniques (PB-relaxation, Sandwich-LN) and finetuning recipes (super-resolution, captioning/self-reranking, style learning, fashion design).

title: SimSwap: An Efficient Framework For High Fidelity Face Swapping
summary: A face swapping framework that generalizes to arbitrary identities by injecting source-identity features (via AdaIN-based ID-Blocks) into target-image features, plus a Weak Feature Matching Loss that implicitly preserves target attributes (paper facts, Sections 1, 3.2, 3.3).

title: Per-Pixel Classification is Not All You Need for Semantic Segmentation
summary: MaskFormer reformulates semantic (and panoptic) segmentation as mask classification: a Transformer decoder with N queries predicts N (class, mask-embedding) pairs whose dot product with per-pixel embeddings yields binary masks, unifying semantic and instance segmentation with one model, loss, and training procedure (paper facts, Sections 1, 3.3).

title: Align before Fuse: Vision and Language Representation Learning with Momentum Distillation
summary: ALBEF aligns unimodal image (ViT-B/16) and text (6-layer BERT) representations with an image-text contrastive loss before fusing them via a 6-layer cross-attention multimodal encoder, and adds momentum distillation (EMA teacher pseudo-targets) to handle noisy web image-text pairs (Section 3, Figure 1).

title: What Matters in Learning from Offline Human Demonstrations for Robot Manipulation
summary: A large empirical study of six offline learning algorithms (BC, BC-RNN, HBC, BCQ, CQL, IRIS) on simulated and real robot manipulation tasks with human demonstration datasets, finding that history-dependent models (especially BC-RNN) excel on human data, batch RL struggles, and observation space, hyperparameters, and policy selection choices matter greatly. (Paraphrase of Sections 1-5.)

title: DRAEM -- A discriminatively trained reconstruction embedding for surface anomaly detection
summary: DRAEM casts surface anomaly detection as a discriminative problem: a reconstructive sub-network inpaints anomalies on synthetically corrupted images, and a U-Net-like discriminative sub-network takes the concatenation of original and reconstructed images to output a per-pixel anomaly map, trained end-to-end on simulated anomalies only (Sections 3-3.2).

title: Robust High-Resolution Video Matting with Temporal Guidance
summary: A real-time human video matting network (per the paper) combining a MobileNetV3-Large/LR-ASPP encoder, a multi-scale ConvGRU recurrent decoder, and a Deep Guided Filter upsampler, trained jointly with matting and human-segmentation objectives for robustness without trimaps or captured backgrounds.

title: LightNER: A Lightweight Tuning Paradigm for Low-resource NER via Pluggable Prompting
summary: A parameter-efficient low-resource NER method that reformulates sequence labeling as seq2seq generation with a pointer network and a unified learnable verbalizer (handling class transfer), plus a pluggable guidance module of learnable key/value prompt parameters inserted into self-attention (handling domain transfer) while keeping the pre-trained LM frozen.

title: Datasets: A Community Library for Natural Language Processing
summary: The paper describes the Hugging Face Datasets library: a community platform standardizing retrieval, typed tabular representation (Apache Arrow), memory-mapped access, streaming, documentation (data cards), and metrics for NLP datasets. It is a data-infrastructure paper, not a model paper.

title: DistilHuBERT: Speech Representation Learning by Layer-wise Distillation of Hidden-unit BERT
summary: A multi-task knowledge distillation framework where a small student (CNN + 2-layer transformer, ~25% of HuBERT's size) uses three prediction heads to regress the teacher HuBERT's 4th, 8th, and 12th hidden-layer outputs, combining L1 and cosine-similarity losses; heads are removed after pre-training and the frozen student serves as a speech representation extractor.

title: OneFlow: Redesign the Distributed Deep Learning Framework from Scratch
summary: OneFlow is a distributed DL training framework redesigned around the SBP (split/broadcast/partial-value) tensor-mapping abstraction and an actor-model runtime, letting the compiler automatically generate physical execution plans for data, model, pipeline, and hybrid parallelism with minimal user effort (paper facts, Sections 1-7).

title: How Well Do Sparse ImageNet Models Transfer?
summary: A systematic empirical study (per Section 2 'Contribution' block) showing that unstructured-pruned ImageNet CNNs (mainly ResNet50, pruned via GMP, WoodFisher, STR, AC/DC, RigL, LTH-T) can match or exceed dense-model transfer accuracy on twelve downstream tasks, with the best pruning method depending on whether linear or full finetuning is used.

title: Godot Reinforcement Learning Agents
summary: An open-source interface (per the paper) connecting the Godot Game Engine to Deep RL frameworks (Ray RLlib, Stable Baselines) via a Gym wrapper, supporting 2D/3D environments with discrete, continuous, and mixed action spaces, parallel actors, and sensors such as raycasts.

title: ICON: Implicit Clothed humans Obtained from Normals
summary: ICON reconstructs detailed 3D clothed humans from a single RGB image by combining SMPL(-X) body priors with local-feature implicit functions: a body-guided normal prediction module (front/back) and a visibility-aware occupancy MLP, plus an inference-time feedback loop that alternately refines the SMPL fit and the predicted normals.

title: GLIDE: Towards Photorealistic Image Generation and Editing with Text-Guided Diffusion Models
summary: The paper trains a 3.5B-parameter text-conditional diffusion model (ADM-style U-Net plus a Transformer text encoder) at 64x64 with a 1.5B upsampler to 256x256, finds classifier-free guidance preferred over noised-CLIP guidance by human evaluators, and fine-tunes the model for text-driven inpainting/editing (Sections 1, 4, 5).

title: Detecting Twenty-thousand Classes using Image-level Supervision
summary: Detic (per the paper) trains a two-stage object detector's classifier on image-level labels by applying a binary cross-entropy loss to the max-size region proposal, expanding detector vocabulary to ~21K classes without prediction-based label assignment.

title: When Shift Operation Meets Vision Transformer: An Extremely Simple Alternative to Attention Mechanism
summary: The paper (per 'Extracted text block 5') replaces the attention layer in a Swin-style hierarchical ViT with a zero-parameter, zero-FLOP partial shift operation that moves a small fraction of channels one pixel along four spatial directions, yielding the ShiftViT backbone that matches or exceeds Swin Transformer on classification, detection, and segmentation.

title: Transformers in Time Series: A Survey
summary: A survey (not a single model) that taxonomizes time-series Transformers by network modifications (positional encoding, attention modules, architecture-level changes) and applications (forecasting, anomaly detection, classification), with empirical analyses on ETTm2 showing robustness degradation with long inputs, best performance at 3-6 layers, and large gains from seasonal-trend decomposition.

title: Highly Accurate Dichotomous Image Segmentation
summary: The paper introduces the DIS task and DIS5K dataset (5,470 high-resolution images with pixel-accurate binary masks), the IS-Net baseline that uses a frozen ground-truth encoder to provide feature-level intermediate supervision on a U2-Net-style segmentation component, and the HCE evaluation metric (per Sections 3, 4, 5 of the paper text).

title: Kubric: A scalable dataset generator
summary: Kubric is an open-source Python framework that interfaces Blender (ray-traced rendering) and PyBullet (physics) to generate photo-realistic synthetic scenes with rich ground-truth annotations (segmentation, depth, optical flow, surface normals, object coordinates, trajectories), scaling to thousands of workers and TBs of data, demonstrated via 13 generated vision datasets/challenges (paper Sections 1-4).

title: DINO: DETR with Improved DeNoising Anchor Boxes for End-to-End Object Detection
summary: DINO is a DETR-like end-to-end object detector that improves DN-DETR/DAB-DETR via contrastive denoising training (CDN), mixed query selection for anchor initialization, and a look-forward-twice box-prediction scheme, achieving 49.4 AP (12 epochs) and 51.3 AP (24 epochs) on COCO with ResNet-50 and 63.3 AP test-dev with SwinL pre-trained on Objects365.

title: Long Time No See! Open-Domain Conversation with Long-Term Persona Memory
summary: The paper proposes the LeMon task, the DuLeMon Chinese mutual-persona dialogue dataset, and PLATO-LTM: a plug-and-play long-term memory (LTM) framework that extracts persona sentences from dialogue in real time, stores user and bot personas in separate memories, retrieves relevant personas via context-persona matching, and conditions a PLATO-2 generator on them, improving long-term dialogue consistency.

title: Competition-Level Code Generation with AlphaCode
summary: AlphaCode is a system for generating Python/C++ solutions to competitive programming problems: an encoder-decoder transformer (with multi-query attention) pre-trained on GitHub code, fine-tuned on the CodeContests dataset with tempering, value conditioning/prediction and GOLD, then large-scale sampling with example-test filtering and behavior-based clustering to select at most 10 submissions (paper Sections 1, 3, 4).

title: A Lightweight Instrument-Agnostic Model for Polyphonic Note Transcription and Multipitch Estimation
summary: The paper proposes NMP, a tiny fully-convolutional network (~16.8k parameters) that takes a harmonic-stacked CQT of audio and jointly predicts frame-level onset, note, and multipitch posteriorgrams, followed by heuristic post-processing to produce note events; it outperforms an instrument-agnostic baseline across several datasets (Sections 3-4).

title: VideoMAE: Masked Autoencoders are Data-Efficient Learners for Self-Supervised Video Pre-Training
summary: VideoMAE is a self-supervised video pre-training method that masks video cubes with an extremely high ratio (90-95%) using tube masking (same mask across all frames) and reconstructs masked pixels with an asymmetric ViT encoder-decoder, enabling data-efficient training of vanilla ViT backbones on small video datasets (per Sections 1, 3.3).

title: Pastiche Master: Exemplar-Based High-Resolution Portrait Style Transfer
summary: DualStyleGAN extends a pre-trained StyleGAN with an extrinsic style path (ModRes blocks for structure, color transform blocks for color) plus progressive fine-tuning and facial destylization, enabling exemplar-based 1024x1024 portrait style transfer with a few hundred style images (paraphrased from Sections 1, 3.2, 3.3).

title: Thin-Plate Spline Motion Model for Image Animation
summary: An unsupervised image-animation framework that estimates motion with thin-plate spline (TPS) transformations plus an affine background transform, uses multi-resolution occlusion masks for feature fusion, and adds auxiliary losses (bg, warp) to improve motion accuracy and inpainting quality (Sections 1, 3).

title: Training Compute-Optimal Large Language Models
summary: The paper empirically derives compute-optimal scaling laws from over 400 training runs, finding that model size and training tokens should scale in equal proportions with compute, and validates this by training Chinchilla (70B parameters, 1.4T tokens), which outperforms larger models like Gopher (280B).

title: Killing Two Birds with One Stone: Efficient and Robust Training of Face Recognition CNNs by Partial FC
summary: The paper proposes Partial FC (PFC), a sparsely updated fully connected layer for large-scale face recognition: all class centers are maintained, but each iteration only positive centers plus a random subset of negative centers (sampling ratio r) are used to compute a margin-based softmax loss, reducing memory, compute, inter-class conflict, and passive updates of tail centers (Sections 1, 3.2).

title: BEVFusion: Multi-Task Multi-Sensor Fusion with Unified Bird's-Eye View Representation
summary: BEVFusion unifies camera and LiDAR features in a shared bird's-eye-view (BEV) space for multi-task 3D perception, with an optimized BEV pooling (precomputation + interval reduction) that speeds camera-to-BEV transformation by over 40x, achieving state-of-the-art nuScenes/Waymo detection and BEV map segmentation.

title: Onesweep: A Faster Least Significant Digit Radix Sort for GPUs
summary: The paper proposes Onesweep, a GPU least-significant-digit radix sort that fuses per-block histogram computation into a single chained-scan binning pass with decoupled look-back, reducing global memory traffic from ~3n to ~2n operations per digit-binning iteration and achieving 29.4 GKey/s on A100 for 256M random 32-bit keys (~1.4-1.6x over CUB 1.10).

title: EnvPool: A Highly Parallel Reinforcement Learning Environment Execution Engine
summary: EnvPool is a C++ thread-pool-based engine that parallelizes RL environment execution with asynchronous send/recv APIs (ActionBufferQueue, ThreadPool, StateBufferQueue), achieving up to 1M FPS on Atari and 3M physics steps/s on MuJoCo on a DGX-A100, with drop-in gym/dm_env compatibility. It is an RL systems-infrastructure paper, not a model-architecture paper.

title: Towards Robust Blind Face Restoration with Codebook Lookup Transformer
summary: CodeFormer casts blind face restoration as code-token prediction in a learned discrete codebook space: a VQ autoencoder learns a 1024-item codebook and decoder on high-quality faces (Stage I), a 9-block Transformer predicts code sequences from degraded-face features (Stage II), and a controllable feature transformation (CFT) module trades fidelity vs. quality (Stage III).

title: XMem: Long-Term Video Object Segmentation with an Atkinson-Shiffrin Memory Model
summary: XMem is a semi-supervised video object segmentation model that maintains three feature memory stores (sensory GRU memory, high-resolution working memory, compact long-term prototype memory) with a memory consolidation/potentiation algorithm and an anisotropic L2 memory-reading similarity, enabling accurate segmentation of very long videos with bounded GPU memory (Sections 1, 3).

title: I Learn to Diffuse, or Data Alchemy 101: a Mnemonic Manifesto
summary: A position/manifesto paper (alt.vis) proposing 'data alchemy' as a narrative device linking visualization, alchemy, and text-to-image diffusion (Disco Diffusion), structured as ten theses presented via a multimedia miro board and comic. It contains no model, algorithm, dataset, or quantitative results.

title: Flow Straight and Fast: Learning to Generate and Transfer Data with Rectified Flow
summary: Rectified flow learns a neural ODE transporting between two distributions by regressing the velocity field onto straight-line directions (X1-X0) via least squares; recursive reflow straightens paths, enabling few/one-step Euler sampling for generation, translation, and domain adaptation.

title: Multi-Granularity Prediction for Scene Text Recognition
summary: MGP-STR: a ViT-based scene text recognizer with an Adaptive Addressing and Aggregation (A3) module, plus a Multi-Granularity Prediction strategy that adds BPE and WordPiece subword classification heads (no separate language model) and fuses the three predictions at decision level.

title: Monolith: Real Time Recommendation System With Collisionless Embedding Table
summary: A production recommendation system (per Section 1/2) built around a collisionless Cuckoo-hash embedding table with frequency filtering and expirable embeddings, plus online training with incremental parameter synchronization and daily-snapshot fault tolerance; the paper shows collisionless embeddings and frequent sync improve online AUC.

title: Efficient Few-Shot Learning Without Prompts
summary: The paper proposes SetFit, a prompt-free few-shot text classification framework: a pretrained Sentence Transformer is first fine-tuned contrastively (Siamese) on sentence pairs, then a logistic regression classification head is trained on the resulting embeddings, achieving competitive few-shot accuracy with much smaller models than prompt-based methods (Sections 3, 5).

title: VToonify: Controllable High-Resolution Portrait Video Style Transfer
summary: A fully convolutional encoder-generator framework that distills StyleGAN-based image toonification models (Toonify, DualStyleGAN) into a video style transfer model supporting unaligned faces, variable frame sizes, high-resolution output, and flexible style/degree control, trained on synthetic paired data with a flicker suppression loss.

title: Human Motion Diffusion Model
summary: MDM is a classifier-free diffusion model for human motion generation that uses a transformer-encoder backbone, predicts the clean sample x0 rather than the noise, and supports geometric losses (position, velocity, foot contact) plus text/action conditioning and inpainting-based editing (Sections 1, 3).

title: Is Reinforcement Learning (Not) for Natural Language Processing: Benchmarks, Baselines, and Building Blocks for Natural Language Policy Optimization
summary: The paper introduces RL4LMs (a library for fine-tuning language generators with on-policy RL), the GRUE benchmark of reward-supervised generation tasks, and NLPO, a PPO variant that learns a top-p token mask via a periodically updated masking policy to stabilize RL fine-tuning of LMs against reward hacking.

title: Evaluate & Evaluation on the Hub: Better Best Practices for Data and Model Measurements
summary: The paper introduces the Evaluate library (canonical, versioned, documented metrics/comparisons/measurements) and the Evaluation on the Hub platform for reproducible, centralized, no-code evaluation of models on datasets. It is an evaluation-tooling paper, not a model architecture paper.

title: Cross-Domain Aspect Extraction using Transformers Augmented with Knowledge Graphs
summary: The paper proposes automatically constructing domain-specific knowledge graphs from ConceptNet plus a COMET-augmented generative source, deciding via syntactic cues when to inject knowledge, and injecting it into pretrained Transformers either by inserting pivot tokens into the input or by a modified DeBERTa disentangled-attention scheme, achieving state-of-the-art cross-domain aspect extraction F1 (Section 1, Section 3).

title: High Fidelity Neural Audio Compression
summary: EnCodec (paper facts): a streaming convolutional encoder-decoder neural audio codec with residual vector quantization, trained end-to-end with reconstruction, multi-scale STFT adversarial, and commitment losses plus a gradient balancer, optionally compressed further by a small Transformer language model with entropy coding.

title: Large-scale Contrastive Language-Audio Pretraining with Feature Fusion and Keyword-to-Caption Augmentation
summary: The paper releases LAION-Audio-630K (633,526 audio-text pairs), builds a CLIP-style contrastive language-audio model (HTSAT/PANN audio encoders, RoBERTa/BERT/CLIP text encoders, 2-layer MLP projections), and adds feature fusion for variable-length audio plus keyword-to-caption augmentation, achieving strong text-to-audio retrieval and zero-shot audio classification (Sections 1-4).

title: Diffusion Models for Medical Image Analysis: A Comprehensive Survey
summary: A survey (per Section 1/Abstract) that taxonomizes diffusion models (DDPM, NCSN, SDE formulations) across nine medical imaging application categories, covering theory, clinical motivation, and open challenges; it is a review, not a single proposed architecture.

title: Galactica: A Large Language Model for Science
summary: Galactica is a family of decoder-only Transformer LLMs (125M–120B) trained on a curated 106B-token scientific corpus with special tokens for citations, reasoning (<work>), SMILES, and protein/DNA sequences, plus prompt pre-training; it achieves strong scientific knowledge, reasoning, and multi-modal results (paper facts).

title: DiffusionDet: Diffusion Model for Object Detection
summary: Formulates object detection as a denoising diffusion process from noisy boxes to object boxes: during training, ground-truth boxes are corrupted with Gaussian noise and a detection decoder learns to predict clean boxes conditioned on image features; at inference, random boxes are progressively refined (with DDIM and box renewal), enabling a dynamic number of boxes and iterative evaluation with the same trained parameters (Sections 1, 3).

title: SmoothQuant: Accurate and Efficient Post-Training Quantization for Large Language Models
summary: A training-free post-training quantization method that migrates activation-quantization difficulty to weights via a mathematically equivalent per-channel scaling transformation, enabling W8A8 INT8 quantization of LLMs with negligible accuracy loss (paper claim).

title: VideoReTalking: Audio-based Lip Synchronization for Talking Head Video Editing In the Wild
summary: A three-stage pipeline (D-Net expression neutralization, L-Net audio-driven lip-sync inpainting, E-Net identity-aware enhancement) that edits talking-head videos to match new audio with emotion control, without per-speaker retraining.

title: DAMO-YOLO : A Report on Real-Time Object Detection Design
summary: A real-time object detector family (DAMO-YOLO) built from a MAE-NAS-searched backbone, a heavy Reparameterized Generalized-FPN (RepGFPN) neck, a minimal ZeroHead (task projection layers only), AlignedOTA dynamic label assignment, and feature-based (CWD) distillation, achieving state-of-the-art COCO accuracy-latency trade-offs.

title: Multi-Concept Customization of Text-to-Image Diffusion
summary: Custom Diffusion: an efficient fine-tuning method that adds new concepts to a pretrained text-to-image diffusion model (Stable Diffusion) by optimizing only key/value projection matrices in cross-attention layers plus a modifier token, with regularization images to prevent forgetting, and supports multi-concept composition via joint training or closed-form constrained merging.

title: RT-1: Robotics Transformer for Real-World Control at Scale
summary: RT-1 is a 35M-parameter vision-language-action policy that tokenizes a history of 6 images (via FiLM-conditioned EfficientNet-B3 and TokenLearner) plus a language instruction, and uses a decoder-only Transformer to output discretized robot action tokens at 3 Hz, trained by behavioral cloning on ~130k real-robot demonstrations over 700+ tasks.

title: Point-E: A System for Generating 3D Point Clouds from Complex Prompts
summary: A fast text-to-3D pipeline (per the paper, Sections 1 and 4) that generates a synthetic view with a fine-tuned GLIDE text-to-image diffusion model, then samples a coarse 1K-point RGB point cloud and upsamples it to 4K points using Transformer-based diffusion models conditioned on CLIP image latent grids, trading sample quality for 1-2 minute sampling instead of GPU-hours.

title: DDColor: Towards Photo-Realistic Image Colorization via Dual Decoders
summary: An end-to-end image colorization network with a pixel decoder (restoring spatial resolution via PixelShuffle upsampling) and a query-based color decoder (learning semantic-aware color queries via cross-attention over multi-scale features), plus a colorfulness loss (paper, Sections 1 and 3).

title: Mastering Diverse Domains through World Models
summary: DreamerV3: a general reinforcement learning algorithm built on an RSSM world model with actor-critic learning from imagined trajectories, using robustness techniques (symlog, symexp twohot, free bits, return normalization, unimix) that enable a single fixed hyperparameter configuration to work across 150+ tasks in 8 domains, including collecting diamonds in Minecraft from scratch.

title: Deep Industrial Image Anomaly Detection: A Survey
summary: A survey (not a method paper) that taxonomizes deep industrial image anomaly detection (IAD) into feature-embedding (teacher-student, one-class classification, distribution-map, memory bank) and reconstruction-based (AE, GAN, Transformer, diffusion) families, reviews supervision levels, datasets, metrics, and industrial settings, and outlines open challenges. Paper facts only; no single novel architecture is proposed.

title: REPLUG: Retrieval-Augmented Black-Box Language Models
summary: REPLUG treats a frozen black-box LM as a scoring function and augments it with a tuneable dense retriever: retrieved documents are each prepended separately to the input and output probabilities are ensembled; REPLUG LSR further trains the retriever using LM perplexity as supervision via a KL objective.

title: GeneFace: Generalized and High-Fidelity Audio-Driven 3D Talking Face Synthesis
summary: A three-stage NeRF-based talking face system: a variational motion generator (VAE with flow-based prior) trained on a large lip-reading corpus maps HuBERT audio features to 3D facial landmarks; a domain-adaptive post-net (semi-supervised adversarial training) adapts landmarks to a target person; a landmark-conditioned head-NeRF plus head-aware torso-NeRF renders high-fidelity frames.

title: Multimodal Chain-of-Thought Reasoning in Language Models
summary: Proposes Multimodal-CoT: a two-stage fine-tuning framework (rationale generation, then answer inference) that fuses frozen ViT vision features with T5 language representations via single-head cross-attention and gated fusion, enabling sub-1B models to produce effective chain-of-thought rationales and achieve state-of-the-art ScienceQA accuracy.

title: 3D-aware Conditional Image Synthesis
summary: Pix2pix3D extends conditional generative models with neural radiance fields: given a 2D label map (segmentation or edge map), it synthesizes photorealistic images from arbitrary viewpoints, jointly predicting 3D color, density, features, and semantic labels, enabling cross-view editing (paper facts from Sections 1 and 3).

title: Composer: Creative and Controllable Image Synthesis with Composable Conditions
summary: A multi-conditional diffusion model (GLIDE-style UNet) trained to reconstruct images from subsets of eight decomposed representations (caption, CLIP embeddings, color histogram, sketch, instance masks, depthmap, grayscale intensity, masked image), enabling composable, controllable image generation and editing without task-specific retraining.

title: Not what you've signed up for: Compromising Real-World LLM-Integrated Applications with Indirect Prompt Injection
summary: The paper introduces Indirect Prompt Injection (IPI): attackers plant natural-language instructions in data that LLM-integrated applications retrieve at inference time, enabling data theft, fraud, worm-like self-spreading prompts, content manipulation, and denial of service. It provides a threat taxonomy and qualitative demonstrations on Bing Chat, GitHub Copilot, and synthetic GPT-4/LangChain applications. It is a security analysis paper, not a

title: Diffusion Policy: Visuomotor Policy Learning via Action Diffusion
summary: Represents a robot visuomotor policy as a conditional denoising diffusion process (DDPM) over action sequences, with receding-horizon control, visual conditioning, and a time-series diffusion transformer, showing large behavior-cloning gains across 15 manipulation tasks (paper claims).

title: Visual ChatGPT: Talking, Drawing and Editing with Visual Foundation Models
summary: A training-free system that wraps ChatGPT with a Prompt Manager and 22 Visual Foundation Models (Stable Diffusion variants, ControlNet, BLIP, MiDaS, detectors) so users can converse with images, and the LLM iteratively dispatches VFMs via chain-of-thought reasoning with strict filename and reasoning-format conventions.

title: Retinexformer: One-stage Retinex-based Transformer for Low-light Image Enhancement
summary: A one-stage Retinex-based framework (ORF) with an Illumination-Guided Transformer (IGT) for low-light image enhancement, where illumination features guide channel-token self-attention (IG-MSA) in a U-shaped restorer.

title: ViperGPT: Visual Inference via Python Execution for Reasoning
summary: ViperGPT (per paper) composes pretrained vision/language models into Python programs: a code-generating LLM (Codex) receives an API specification plus a visual query, generates a Python function, and a Python interpreter executes it on the image/video using modules like GLIP (find), X-VLM (verify_property, best_text_match), MiDaS (compute_depth), BLIP-2 (simple_query), and GPT-3 (llm_query/select_answer). It is training-free and achieves zero-sho

title: ChatDoctor: A Medical Chat Model Fine-tuned on LLaMA Model using Medical Domain Knowledge
summary: Fine-tunes LLaMA-7B (after Alpaca-style instruction tuning) on 100k real patient-physician dialogues and adds a prompt-driven retrieval mechanism over an offline disease database and online sources to improve medical chatbot accuracy.

title: CodeGeeX: A Pre-Trained Model for Code Generation with Multilingual Evaluations on HumanEval-X
summary: CodeGeeX is a 13B-parameter GPT-style decoder-only code generation model pre-trained on 850B tokens across 23 programming languages, and the paper introduces HumanEval-X, a multilingual benchmark (820 problem-solution pairs in C++, Java, JavaScript, Go, Python) for evaluating code generation and translation via functional correctness (pass@k).

title: Beyond Appearance: a Semantic Controllable Self-Supervised Learning Framework for Human-Centric Visual Tasks
summary: SOLIDER (per Sections 1, 3): a self-supervised framework that derives pseudo semantic labels for human-image tokens via magnitude-based foreground clustering plus y-axis-position-based semantic clustering, adds a token-level semantic classification pretext task (with masked semantic supervision) to DINO, and inserts a semantic controller (FiLM-like conditioning on a continuous value λ) after each Swin block so downstream tasks can trade off seman

title: Dataset and Baseline System for Multi-lingual Extraction and Normalization of Temporal and Numerical Expressions
summary: The paper introduces NTX, a manually annotated multi-lingual dataset (14 languages, 26000+ sentences) covering extraction, normalization, and resolution of 8 numerical and 10 temporal entity sub-types, plus a rule-based baseline system (Recognizers-Text). It proposes no neural model; the baseline is deterministic regex/dictionary rules with cascaded parsers.

title: Vision-Language Models for Vision Tasks: A Survey
summary: A survey (not a single model) systematizing VLM pre-training, transfer learning, and knowledge distillation for visual recognition, covering architectures, objectives, datasets, benchmarks, and future directions.

title: ImageReward: Learning and Evaluating Human Preferences for Text-to-Image Generation
summary: The paper introduces ImageReward, the first general-purpose text-to-image human preference reward model trained on 137k expert comparison pairs, and ReFL, a direct fine-tuning algorithm that optimizes latent diffusion models against the reward model's scores (paraphrase of Sections 1-3).

title: Low-code LLM: Graphical User Interface over Large Language Models
summary: A human-LLM interaction framework where a Planning LLM produces a structured, editable workflow (flowchart) that users refine via six low-code visual operations, and an Executing LLM generates responses following the confirmed workflow (per Sections 1-2).

title: Efficient and Effective Text Encoding for Chinese LLaMA and Alpaca
summary: The paper extends LLaMA's vocabulary with 20,000 Chinese tokens, continues pre-training on Chinese corpora with LoRA, and applies supervised instruction fine-tuning to produce Chinese LLaMA (foundation) and Chinese Alpaca (instruction-following) models with improved Chinese encoding efficiency and task performance.

title: Phoenix: Democratizing ChatGPT across Languages
summary: The paper fine-tunes multilingual pre-trained backbones (BLOOMZ for Phoenix, LLaMA for Chimera) on a mix of translated multilingual instruction data and ChatGPT-distilled conversation data, producing open 7B chat models competitive in Chinese and superior in many non-Latin languages (Sections 1.1, 3.1, 5).

title: Track Anything: Segment Anything Meets Videos
summary: A training-free interactive pipeline (TAM) combining SAM for click-based mask initialization/refinement and XMem for temporal mask propagation in videos, with human correction during one-pass inference.

title: Harnessing the Power of LLMs in Practice: A Survey on ChatGPT and Beyond
summary: A practitioner-oriented survey (not a model paper) categorizing LLMs into BERT-style encoder and GPT-style decoder families and giving guidance on when to use LLMs vs. fine-tuned models across data regimes and NLP tasks. It specifies no novel architecture, training procedure, or reproducible model.

title: Is Your Code Generated by ChatGPT Really Correct? Rigorous Evaluation of Large Language Models for Code Generation
summary: The paper proposes EvalPlus, an evaluation framework that augments code-generation benchmarks (notably HumanEval, yielding HumanEval+ and HumanEval+-Mini) with automatically generated test inputs via LLM-based seed generation plus type-aware mutation, uses differential testing against ground-truth implementations, and optionally reduces test suites via greedy set cover over branch coverage, mutant killings, and LLM sample killings. It is an evalu

title: Shap-E: Generating Conditional 3D Implicit Functions
summary: A two-stage conditional generative model for 3D assets: a transformer encoder maps point clouds and multiview renderings to parameters of an implicit MLP (NeRF + signed texture field), and a transformer-based diffusion model generates those latents conditioned on text or images (paraphrase of Sections 1 and 4).

title: Caption Anything: Interactive Image Description with Diverse Multimodal Controls
summary: A training-free controllable image captioning framework (CAT) that composes frozen foundation models — SAM for region segmentation from point/box/trajectory prompts, BLIP-2 for zero-shot captioning with a visual chain-of-thought, and ChatGPT (or open LLMs) as a text refiner for language controls (sentiment, length, language, factuality), plus extensions to object-centric chatting and paragraph captioning.

title: Personalize Segment Anything Model with One Shot
summary: PerSAM personalizes the Segment Anything Model (SAM) for user-specific visual concepts using a single reference image and mask: a training-free variant injects target semantics via a location confidence map, target-guided attention, and target-semantic prompting; PerSAM-F adds a scale-aware fine-tuning of only 2 parameters to aggregate three-scale masks.

title: Otter: A Multi-Modal Model with In-Context Instruction Tuning
summary: Otter is a Flamingo-style multimodal model (CLIP ViT-L/14 vision encoder + MPT-7B decoder connected via a perceiver resampler and cross-gated attention) instruction-tuned on MIMIC-IT, a 3M-pair multimodal instruction dataset with in-context examples, improving convergence, generalization, and video/multi-image understanding.

title: MultiModal-GPT: A Vision and Language Model for Dialogue with Humans
summary: Fine-tunes OpenFlamingo (CLIP vision encoder + perceiver resampler + LLaMA decoder with gated cross-attention) via LoRA on self-attention, cross-attention, and FFN, using a unified instruction template to jointly train on vision-language and language-only instruction data for multi-round dialogue (Sections 2-3).

title: Code Execution with Pre-trained Language Models
summary: The paper introduces CodeExecutor, a 12-layer Transformer (UniXcoder-based, encoder-decoder mode) that learns to predict Python execution traces (line order plus variable states) via a code-execution pre-training objective, supported by a mutation-based dataset (CodeNetMut, SingleLine, Tutorial) and curriculum learning from easy to hard programs.

title: InternChat: Solving Vision-Centric Tasks by Interacting with Chatbots Beyond Language
summary: InternGPT (iGPT) is an interactive framework combining pointing (click/drag/draw) and language instructions: a perception unit (SAM, OCR) parses gestures, an LLM controller (ChatGPT/GPT-4/LLaMA) with an auxiliary control mechanism plans and invokes an open-world toolkit of vision/vision-language APIs, plus Husky, a BLIP-2-style 7B vision-language model fine-tuned for multi-modal dialogue.

title: VideoChat: Chat-Centric Video Understanding
summary: Proposes a chat-centric video understanding system combining video foundation models and LLMs via a learnable neural interface (VideoChat-Embed), plus a text-pipelined variant (VideoChat-Text), and a video-centric instruction dataset emphasizing spatiotemporal reasoning and causality.

title: Segment and Track Anything
summary: SAM-Track unifies interactive video object segmentation by combining SAM (key-frame interactive segmentation), DeAOT (multi-object tracking with hierarchical gated propagation), and Grounding-DINO (text-driven open-set detection), supporting click/box/text interaction and automatic discovery of new objects via a Comparing Mask Results (CMR) rule.

title: EfficientViT: Memory Efficient Vision Transformer with Cascaded Group Attention
summary: The paper proposes EfficientViT, a family of fast vision transformers built from a 'sandwich layout' block (one MHSA between FFN layers), a cascaded group attention (CGA) module that feeds each head a different split of the features and cascades head outputs, and a parameter reallocation strategy (small Q/K, large V, FFN expansion ratio 2), achieving state-of-the-art speed/accuracy trade-offs on ImageNet-1K.

title: Better speech synthesis through scaling
summary: TorToise: a multi-voice TTS system combining an autoregressive GPT-2-style decoder over discrete speech tokens, a CLIP-like contrastive re-ranker (CLVP), a DDPM that decodes speech tokens/AR latents to MEL spectrograms, and a Univnet vocoder, trained on ~49k hours of scraped speech (per paper).

title: CodeT5+: Open Code Large Language Models for Code Understanding and Generation
summary: A family of encoder-decoder code LLMs (220M–16B) that can flexibly operate in encoder-only, decoder-only, or encoder-decoder modes, trained with a mixture of pretraining objectives (span denoising, causal LM, text-code contrastive learning, matching) on unimodal and bimodal data, plus compute-efficient scaling by freezing off-the-shelf decoder LLMs and instruction tuning.

title: C-Eval: A Multi-Level Multi-Discipline Chinese Evaluation Suite for Foundation Models
summary: The paper introduces C-Eval, a Chinese multiple-choice evaluation benchmark of 13,948 questions across 52 subjects and four difficulty levels, plus C-Eval HARD, and reports that only GPT-4 exceeds 60% average accuracy. It is a benchmark/evaluation paper, not a model architecture paper.

title: Tree of Thoughts: Deliberate Problem Solving with Large Language Models
summary: The paper proposes Tree of Thoughts (ToT), an inference-time framework that generalizes chain-of-thought prompting: a pre-trained LM generates multiple intermediate 'thoughts' per step, self-evaluates them via value or vote prompts, and a search algorithm (BFS or DFS) explores, prunes, and backtracks over the resulting tree. No new model is trained; the framework is evaluated with GPT-4/GPT-3.5 on Game of 24, Creative Writing, and Mini Crosswords

title: Drag Your GAN: Interactive Point-based Manipulation on the Generative Image Manifold
summary: DragGAN enables interactive point-based editing of GAN-generated images by (1) a feature-based motion supervision loss that optimizes the latent code to move handle points toward targets, and (2) point tracking via nearest-neighbor search in the GAN's intermediate feature maps, requiring no auxiliary networks (paper Sections 1, 3).

title: VisionLLM: Large Language Model is also an Open-Ended Decoder for Vision-Centric Tasks
summary: VisionLLM unifies vision-centric tasks (detection, segmentation, grounding, captioning, VQA) under language instructions, using a language-guided image tokenizer and an LLM-based open-ended task decoder with vocabulary-expanded location/class tokens and output-format-as-query decoding (paper facts).

title: QUEST: A Retrieval Dataset of Entity-Seeking Queries with Implicit Set Operations
summary: The paper introduces QUEST, a dataset of 3357 natural language queries with implicit set operations (intersection, union, difference) over Wikipedia entity documents, built semi-automatically from Wikipedia categories with crowdworker paraphrasing, validation, relevance labeling, and attribution. Baselines (BM25 and T5 dual encoders plus T5 cross-attention classifiers) perform poorly, especially on negation and conjunction (Sections 1, 3, 4).

title: Any-to-Any Generation via Composable Diffusion
summary: CoDi (per the paper) aligns modality-specific prompt encoders via 'Bridging Alignment' and aligns latent diffusion models via 'Latent Alignment' with environment encoders and cross-attention, enabling any-to-any generation across text, image, video, and audio with a linear number of training objectives.

title: RWKV: Reinventing RNNs for the Transformer Era
summary: RWKV is an RNN/Transformer hybrid language model that replaces quadratic dot-product attention with a channel-wise time-decay WKV operator, enabling parallelizable training and constant-memory RNN-style inference; models up to 14B parameters were trained on the Pile.

title: Know Your Self-supervised Learning: A Survey on Image-based Generative and Discriminative Training
summary: A survey (not a model paper) that taxonomizes ~100 image-based self-supervised learning frameworks into generative (GAN-based, masked image modeling) and discriminative (clustering, contrastive, distillation, information-maximization) families, describes pretext tasks, core concepts (Siamese backbones, stop-grad, momentum/EMA teachers, projector/predictor MLPs), loss functions (InfoNCE, MSE, MAE, VicReg), and evaluation protocols (linear probing,

title: Enhancing Chat Language Models by Scaling High-quality Instructional Conversations
summary: The paper introduces UltraChat, a 1.5M multi-turn instructional conversation dataset generated without human queries via iterative user/assistant LLM simulation across three sectors, and UltraLLaMA, a LLaMA-13B model fine-tuned on it, which reportedly outperforms open-source baselines like Vicuna (paraphrased from Sections 1-6).

title: WikiChat: Stopping the Hallucination of Large Language Model Chatbots by Few-Shot Grounding on Wikipedia
summary: A 7-stage few-shot pipeline that grounds LLM chatbot responses in Wikipedia via retrieval, claim extraction, and fact-checking, plus distillation of the GPT-4-based pipeline into a 7B LLaMA student, achieving ~97% factual accuracy with low latency (paraphrased from Sections 1-4).

title: QLoRA: Efficient Finetuning of Quantized LLMs
summary: The paper introduces QLoRA, a finetuning method that backpropagates through a frozen 4-bit quantized LLM (using NF4 data type, double quantization, and paged optimizers) into Low-Rank Adapters, matching 16-bit finetuning quality; its Guanaco chatbots were trained this way on OASST1.

title: Optimal Linear Subspace Search: Learning to Construct Fast and High-Quality Schedulers for Diffusion Models
summary: OLSS reformulates diffusion scheduler design as learning coefficients of a linear iterative formula via least squares over recorded intermediate variables, plus a binary-search path optimization over sampling steps, enabling high-quality few-step image generation (paper claim, Sections 3.3-3.4).

title: Voyager: An Open-Ended Embodied Agent with Large Language Models
summary: Voyager is a prompt-based, gradient-free LLM agent system for Minecraft combining an automatic curriculum, an embedding-indexed skill library of executable code, and an iterative prompting loop with environment feedback, execution errors, and self-verification. It involves no model training; it queries GPT-4/GPT-3.5 as black-box APIs.

title: Chain-of-Thought Hub: A Continuous Effort to Measure Large Language Models' Reasoning Performance
summary: The paper (per 'Extracted text block 15': 'In this work, we consider the evaluation of complex reasoning.') proposes an open-source evaluation suite of six reasoning benchmarks (GSM8k, MATH, MMLU, BigBench Hard, HumanEval, C-Eval) used with few-shot chain-of-thought prompting to compare ~19 LLMs, finding that reasoning correlates with model scale and that leading models are RLHF-tuned. It is an evaluation/benchmarking paper, not a model-architect

title: PyPOTS: A Python Toolkit for Machine Learning on Partially-Observed Time Series
summary: PyPOTS is an open-source Python library (paper facts) providing a unified interface for 52 algorithms across five tasks on partially-observed multivariate time series: imputation, forecasting, anomaly detection, classification, and clustering, with software-engineering guarantees (CI/CD, testing, lazy loading, multi-GPU, NNI hyperparameter tuning). It is a toolkit/survey paper, not a single-model architecture paper.

title: Let's Verify Step by Step
summary: The paper shows that process supervision (step-level feedback) trains more reliable math reward models than outcome supervision (final-answer feedback), that active learning improves data efficiency ~2.6x, and releases the PRM800K dataset of 800K step-level human labels.

title: Humans in 4D: Reconstructing and Tracking Humans with Transformers
summary: Proposes HMR 2.0, a fully transformer-based human mesh recovery network (ViT encoder + transformer decoder regressing SMPL pose/shape/camera), and 4DHumans, a PHALP-based 3D tracking system using a masked pose-prediction transformer, achieving state-of-the-art pose reconstruction and tracking (paper claims).

title: CodeTF: One-stop Transformer Library for State-of-the-art Code LLM
summary: CodeTF is an open-source library (not a single model) that unifies loading, fine-tuning, serving, and evaluation of pretrained Code LLMs across encoder-only, decoder-only, and encoder-decoder families, adding code-specific utilities (tree-sitter AST parsing for 15+ languages) and standardized benchmark evaluation (HumanEval, MBPP, APPS, CodeXGLUE) with metrics like pass@k and CodeBLEU.

title: Bytes Are All You Need: Transformers Operating Directly On File Bytes
summary: ByteFormer (per paper, Sections 1 and 3.1) classifies files directly from raw file bytes using a learned byte embedding, strided 1D convolution, positional embeddings, and a Transformer with shifted window attention and downsampling layers, removing modality-specific preprocessing at inference time.

title: LLaVA-Med: Training a Large Language-and-Vision Assistant for Biomedicine in One Day
summary: The paper adapts the general-domain LLaVA multimodal chatbot to biomedicine via a two-stage curriculum: (1) concept-feature alignment on 600K PMC-15M figure-caption pairs updating only the projection layer, then (2) end-to-end instruction tuning on 60K GPT-4 self-instructed biomedical conversations (60K-IM with inline mentions), training in under 15 hours on eight A100s and achieving strong biomedical VQA results (Sections 3-5).

title: Segment Anything in High Quality
summary: HQ-SAM upgrades SAM for high-quality zero-shot segmentation by adding a learnable HQ-Output Token and a global-local feature fusion, training only ~0.5% extra parameters on a 44K-mask dataset while freezing SAM.

title: Video-LLaMA: An Instruction-tuned Audio-Visual Language Model for Video Understanding
summary: A multi-modal framework that connects frozen LLMs to both video frames and audio via two Q-Former-based branches (vision-language and audio-language), trained with multi-branch cross-modal pre-training followed by visual instruction tuning (paraphrased from Sections 1-2).

title: Neuralangelo: High-Fidelity Neural Surface Reconstruction
summary: A neural surface reconstruction method combining multi-resolution hash encoding with SDF-based volume rendering, using numerical gradients for higher-order derivatives and coarse-to-fine hash-grid activation to recover detailed 3D surfaces from multi-view RGB images.

title: Recognize Anything: A Strong Image Tagging Model
summary: RAM is a large-scale image tagging foundation model trained on annotation-free image-text pairs: tags are parsed from captions, a data engine generates and cleans tags, and a Tag2Text-style architecture with CLIP-text-encoded label queries achieves zero-shot open-vocabulary tagging (Section 2, Extracted text blocks 31-32).

title: How Far Can Camels Go? Exploring the State of Instruction Tuning on Open Resources
summary: A systematic study of instruction-tuning open LLMs (6.7B-65B, mainly LLaMA) on 12 open instruction datasets, with multi-facet evaluation (benchmarks, GPT-4-based, human), introducing TÜLU, LLaMA finetuned on a Human+GPT data mixture (paper facts).

title: Simple and Controllable Music Generation
summary: MusicGen is a single-stage autoregressive transformer language model over EnCodec RVQ audio tokens that generates 32 kHz music conditioned on text or melody, using codebook interleaving patterns (notably the delay pattern) to model multiple parallel token streams without cascaded models (Sections 2.1-2.4).

title: Tracking Everything Everywhere All at Once
summary: OmniMotion is a per-video test-time optimization that represents a video with a quasi-3D canonical volume and per-frame invertible local-canonical bijections (Real-NVP style), enabling dense, globally consistent, long-range pixel trajectories that persist through occlusions (Sections 1, 3, 4).

title: Video-ChatGPT: Towards Detailed Video Understanding via Large Vision and Language Models
summary: A multimodal video conversation model (Video-ChatGPT) that combines a CLIP ViT-L/14 visual encoder adapted for video via temporal and spatial average pooling with a Vicuna-7B LLM, trained by tuning only a linear projection layer on 100K video-instruction pairs, plus a quantitative video-dialogue evaluation benchmark.

title: Judging LLM-as-a-judge with MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena
summary: The paper systematically studies using strong LLMs (e.g., GPT-4) as automated judges of chatbot quality, introduces the MT-bench multi-turn question set and the Chatbot Arena crowdsourced preference platform, documents judge biases (position, verbosity, self-enhancement, weak math/reasoning grading), and shows GPT-4 judges reach >80% agreement with human preferences.

title: FinGPT: Open-Source Financial Large Language Models
summary: An open-source, data-centric framework for financial LLMs: real-time financial data curation, lightweight LoRA/QLoRA fine-tuning of open LLMs (e.g., Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct), RLSP alignment using stock-price reactions, and financial sentiment analysis benchmarks (Sections 3, 5).

title: High-Fidelity Audio Compression with Improved RVQGAN
summary: A universal neural audio codec (Improved RVQGAN) combining a convolutional encoder-decoder with residual vector quantization, Snake periodic activations, factorized/L2-normalized codebooks, multi-scale mel reconstruction, and multi-period plus multi-band multi-scale complex-STFT discriminators, achieving ~90x compression of 44.1 kHz audio at 8 kbps (per paper Sections 1, 3, 4).

title: Data-Copilot: Bridging Billions of Data and Humans with Autonomous Workflow
summary: A code-centric LLM agent that pre-explores data sources to design, test, and optimize reusable code interfaces, then invokes them in workflows (serial/parallel/loop, or hybrid with raw code) to answer real-time data analysis requests with higher accuracy and lower token cost.

title: WebGLM: Towards An Efficient Web-Enhanced Question Answering System with Human Preferences
summary: A web-enhanced long-form QA system built on GLM-10B combining a two-stage LLM-augmented retriever (web search + fine-tuned Contriever), a bootstrapped generator trained on LLM-generated cited QA data (WebGLM-QA), and a human preference-aware scorer trained from forum thumb-ups for best-of-n answer selection (paraphrase of Sections 1 and 3).

title: Rerender A Video: Zero-Shot Text-Guided Video-to-Video Translation
summary: A zero-shot, training-free framework that adapts pre-trained image diffusion models (Stable Diffusion + ControlNet) to text-guided video-to-video translation using hierarchical cross-frame constraints (cross-frame attention, shape/pixel-aware latent fusion, AdaIN color adjustment) plus Ebsynth-based propagation of key frames to non-key frames (Sections 1, 4).

title: h2oGPT: Democratizing Large Language Models
summary: An open-source ecosystem (per Section 2 and Section 3) that fine-tunes permissively licensed foundation LLMs (7B-40B parameters, e.g., GPT-NeoX-20B, Falcon-40B) on curated conversational data (Open Assistant) using LoRA and bitsandbytes quantization, plus chatbot UI, VectorDB-based private document chat, and the no-code H2O LLM Studio fine-tuning framework.

title: INT2.1: Towards Fine-Tunable Quantized Large Language Models with Error Correction through Low-Rank Adaptation
summary: The paper proposes EMEF, a memory-efficient fine-tuning scheme that freezes GPTQ-quantized LLaMA weights and trains injected LoRA low-rank matrices, plus LREC, an error-correction method that trains LoRA adapters against a full-precision teacher using a KL + cross-entropy loss, yielding a functional INT2.1-effective-precision LLaMA 7B (paper Sections 1, 3, 4).

title: WizardCoder: Empowering Code Large Language Models with Evol-Instruct
summary: Introduces Code Evol-Instruct, an automated pipeline that iteratively increases the complexity of code instruction data (constraints, erroneous-code adversarial samples, time/space complexity requirements), then fine-tunes StarCoder 15B and CodeLlama-34B-Python on the evolved data to produce WizardCoder models with state-of-the-art open-source code generation results (paper's claims).

title: Macaw-LLM: Multi-Modal Language Modeling with Image, Audio, Video, and Text Integration
summary: A multi-modal instruction-tuned LLM (per Sections 3.1-3.4) that encodes image/video with CLIP-ViT-B/16 and audio with Whisper-base, aligns those features to a LLaMA-7B embedding space via 1D-conv compression plus attention-based alignment, and trains everything in a single-stage instruction fine-tuning on a GPT-3.5-generated 150K-example dataset.

title: Scaling Open-Vocabulary Object Detection
summary: The paper introduces OWLv2 and the OWL-ST self-training recipe: an existing OWL-ViT open-vocabulary detector pseudo-annotates ~10B WebLI image-text pairs (queries from caption N-grams), a new detector is trained on these pseudo-boxes with efficiency tricks (token dropping, objectness-based instance selection, mosaics), and optional brief fine-tuning on human detection data yields state-of-the-art open-vocabulary detection, scaling to over 1B exam

title: Fast Segment Anything
summary: FastSAM reformulates the Segment Anything task as all-instance segmentation followed by prompt-guided selection, using a YOLOv8-seg CNN detector trained on 2% of SA-1B, achieving comparable performance to SAM at ~50x faster inference (Sections 1, 3, 4).

title: FFCV: Accelerating Training by Removing Data Bottlenecks
summary: FFCV is a data-loading/training-system library (not a model architecture) that removes data bottlenecks via a page-organized .beton file format, OS/process caching, quasi-random sampling, JIT-compiled augmentation pipelines, and multithreaded asynchronous transfer, enabling fast ImageNet training (e.g., ResNet-50 to 75% in ~20 min on 8 A100s).

title: LightGlue: Local Feature Matching at Light Speed
summary: LightGlue is a sparse feature matcher that revisits SuperGlue's Transformer design: rotary relative positional encoding in self-attention, bidirectional cross-attention, a lightweight double-softmax assignment head with unary matchability (replacing Sinkhorn optimal transport), deep supervision at every layer, and adaptive depth (early exit via a confidence classifier) plus adaptive width (pruning confidently unmatchable points), yielding faster,

title: Faster Segment Anything: Towards Lightweight SAM for Mobile Applications
summary: Proposes decoupled distillation: distill SAM's ViT-H image encoder into a tiny ViT (TinyViT-style, ~5.78M params) using MSE on image embeddings, keeping the original lightweight mask decoder, yielding MobileSAM that trains on one GPU in under a day and matches original SAM quality.

title: MotionGPT: Human Motion as a Foreign Language
