summary: A unified motion-language model that quantizes 3D human motion into discrete tokens via a VQ-VAE motion tokenizer, extends a pre-trained T5 vocabulary with motion tokens, and applies two-stage motion-language pre-training plus instruction tuning to handle text-to-motion, motion captioning, motion prediction, and motion in-between with one model (paper Sections 3.1-3.3).

title: 3D-Speaker: A Large-Scale Multi-Device, Multi-Distance, and Multi-Dialect Corpus for Speech Representation Disentanglement
summary: The paper introduces 3D-Speaker, a public speech corpus of 10,000+ speakers (579,013 utterances, ~1124 hours) with labels for recording device, source-to-device distance, and dialect, enabling research on disentangled speech representations, plus baseline speaker-verification benchmarks (ECAPA-TDNN, CAM++, ERes2Net) and dialect-identification and self-supervised baselines.

title: ChatLaw: Open-Source Legal Large Language Model with Integrated External Knowledge Bases (RA-MoE multi-agent legal assistant)
summary: The paper proposes Chatlaw, a multi-agent legal assistant built on a Role-Aligned Mixture-of-Experts (RA-MoE) LLM: a router conditioned on token, agent-role, and knowledge-graph embeddings selects task-specialized experts, trained with a routing loss alongside autoregressive cross-entropy, orchestrated by a four-agent SOP workflow (Legal Assistant, Researcher, Editor, Senior Lawyer) over a curated Chinese legal dataset with a knowledge graph.

title: An Efficient Sparse Inference Software Accelerator for Transformer-based Language Models on CPUs
summary: The paper proposes a CPU inference software stack for Transformer language models with 4x1 block-structured weight sparsity and INT8 quantization, built on a JIT-compiled SpMM kernel using Intel VNNI instructions, plus sparse attention, operator fusion, LUT-based low-precision element-wise ops, and runtime optimizations, evaluated on BERT variants (paper facts).

title: End-to-end Autonomous Driving: Challenges and Frontiers
summary: A survey of 270+ papers on end-to-end autonomous driving, covering imitation/reinforcement learning methods, closed- and open-loop benchmarking, and challenges such as causal confusion, robustness, interpretability, and world models. It proposes no concrete trainable architecture, dataset, or hyperparameters.

title: One-2-3-45: Any Single Image to 3D Mesh in 45 Seconds without Per-Shape Optimization
summary: A feed-forward pipeline that lifts a single image to a 360-degree textured 3D mesh by combining the Zero123 view-conditioned diffusion model, an elevation estimation module, and a SparseNeuS-style SDF-based generalizable reconstruction module trained with 2-stage source view selection and groundtruth-prediction mixed training (per Sections 3.1-3.4).

title: ChatGPT for Robotics: Design Principles and Model Abilities
summary: An empirical study (per Section 1) showing that a dialog-based LLM (ChatGPT) can solve robotics tasks zero-shot when given a high-level function library, structured prompts (XML tags, code prompting), and user-on-the-loop dialog correction; it also releases the PromptCraft platform and an AirSim-ChatGPT simulator integration. It is a prompting/systems study, not a new model architecture or training method.

title: Magic123: One Image to High-Quality 3D Object Generation Using Both 2D and 3D Diffusion Priors
summary: A two-stage coarse-to-fine image-to-3D pipeline that optimizes a NeRF then a DMTet mesh, guided jointly by 2D (Stable Diffusion SDS) and 3D (Zero-1-to-3 SDS) diffusion priors with a trade-off parameter, plus textual inversion and monocular depth regularization.

title: EmoGen: Eliminating Subjective Bias in Emotional Music Generation
summary: EmoGen (per paper) avoids subjective bias in emotion-labeled music generation by using emotion-related music attributes as a bridge: a supervised clustering stage maps emotion labels to representative attribute values, and a self-supervised autoregressive Transformer (Linear Transformer) generates music conditioned on those attributes.

title: SDXL: Improving Latent Diffusion Models for High-Resolution Image Synthesis
summary: SDXL is a latent diffusion text-to-image model with a 2.6B-parameter UNet, dual text encoders (CLIP ViT-L + OpenCLIP ViT-bigG), micro-conditioning on original image size and crop coordinates, multi-aspect-ratio training, an improved autoencoder, and an optional SDEdit-style refinement stage (per Sections 2.1-2.5).

title: A Survey on Evaluation of Large Language Models
summary: A survey (not a model paper) that organizes LLM evaluation research along three dimensions — what to evaluate (tasks), where to evaluate (datasets/benchmarks), and how to evaluate (automatic and human protocols) — and lists grand challenges for LLM evaluation. It proposes no new architecture, training procedure, or reproducible model.

title: VideoGLUE: Video General Understanding Evaluation of Foundation Models
summary: A benchmark (not a new model) that evaluates seven vision/multimodal foundation models on video understanding via three tasks (action recognition, temporal localization, spatiotemporal localization), eight datasets, and four adaptation methods (end-to-end finetuning, frozen backbone, multi-layer attention pooler, low-rank adapter), plus a cost-weighted VideoGLUE Score. Paper facts only; no reproduction is proposed.

title: Focused Transformer: Contrastive Training for Context Scaling
summary: The paper identifies the 'distraction issue' (attention mass spreading evenly over relevant and irrelevant keys in long multi-document contexts) and proposes the Focused Transformer (FoT): a subset of attention layers gains access to an external memory of (key, value) pairs via kNN lookup, trained with a 'crossbatch' procedure where queries differentiably attend to previous context of their own document (positives) and contexts from other documen

title: Semantic-SAM: Segment and Recognize Anything at Any Granularity
summary: A universal image segmentation model that, given a point or box prompt, predicts masks at multiple granularities with object- and part-level semantics, via multi-choice learning (K=6 content prompts per click), many-to-many Hungarian matching, decoupled object/part classification with a shared text encoder, and joint training on SA-1B plus generic and part segmentation datasets (paper Sections 1-3).

title: CoTracker: It is Better to Track Together
summary: CoTracker is a transformer-based point tracker that tracks many 2D points jointly in video via factorized time/track attention with proxy tokens, sliding-window causal inference with unrolled recurrent training, and support points for context (Sections 1, 3).

title: AnyDoor: Zero-shot Object-level Image Customization
summary: AnyDoor is a diffusion-based image generator that teleports a target object into a scene at a user-specified location, zero-shot, by combining identity tokens from a self-supervised encoder (DINOv2) with high-frequency detail maps injected into a pre-trained Stable Diffusion UNet (paraphrase of Sections 1-3).

title: Efficient Guided Generation for Large Language Models
summary: The paper reformulates regex/CFG-guided LLM text generation as finite-state machine (FSM) state tracking, and pre-builds an index mapping FSM states to vocabulary subsets so that per-step token masking costs O(1) on average instead of O(N) over the vocabulary; it extends the idea to PDA/LALR(1) parser-guided generation (Sections 1-4).

title: TokenFlow: Consistent Diffusion Features for Consistent Video Editing
summary: A training-free framework for text-driven video editing that enforces temporal consistency by propagating diffusion self-attention tokens across frames using nearest-neighbor correspondences computed from the original video's diffusion features, alternating keyframe joint editing with token propagation at each denoising step (paper Sections 1, 4).

title: Meta-Transformer: A Unified Framework for Multimodal Learning
summary: Proposes a framework that tokenizes 12 data modalities into a shared token space and encodes them with a single frozen ViT backbone pretrained on LAION-2B, training only lightweight tokenizers and task-specific MLP heads on unpaired data.

title: WebArena: A Realistic Web Environment for Building Autonomous Agents
summary: A self-hostable, reproducible web environment (four functional websites plus tools and knowledge resources) and an 812-task benchmark evaluating autonomous LLM agents on functional correctness of long-horizon web tasks; best GPT-4 agent reaches 14.41% success vs 78.24% human.

title: MiDaS v3.1 -- A Model Zoo for Robust Monocular Relative Depth Estimation
summary: The paper extends the MiDaS monocular relative depth estimation family by integrating new vision transformer backbones (BEiT, Swin, SwinV2, Next-ViT, LeViT) into the MiDaS encoder-decoder architecture, describing hook-based encoder-decoder connection, a two-stage training protocol on mixed disparity datasets, and a general recipe for adding future backbones (Sections 3.2-3.4).

title: Effective Whole-body Pose Estimation with Two-stages Distillation
summary: DWPose: a two-stage knowledge-distillation framework (feature+logit distillation with weight decay, then head-only self-distillation) plus UBody data to improve RTMPose-based whole-body pose estimation on COCO-WholeBody.

title: Do LLMs Possess a Personality? Making the MBTI Test an Amazing Evaluation for Large Language Models
summary: The paper (per Sections 1, 3-5) uses the 93-question MBTI multiple-choice test as a rough evaluation for LLMs by comparing next-token probabilities of options 'A'/'B', finding that LLMs exhibit diverse personality-like types, that prompt engineering changes types only for instruction-tuned models, and that training corpus type shifts T/F and J/P dichotomies. It is an evaluation/analysis study, not a new model architecture.

title: ToolLLM: Facilitating Large Language Models to Master 16000+ Real-world APIs
summary: ToolLLM is a framework for tool use: it builds ToolBench (16,464 real REST APIs, ChatGPT-generated instructions, DFSDT-annotated solution paths), fine-tunes LLaMA-2 7B into ToolLLaMA, trains a Sentence-BERT API retriever, and introduces the ToolEval evaluator (pass rate / win rate).

title: DeepSpeed-Chat: Easy, Fast and Affordable RLHF Training of ChatGPT-like Models at All Scales
summary: A system paper (per Section 1/Abstract) presenting DeepSpeed-Chat: an end-to-end RLHF training pipeline replicating InstructGPT's three steps (SFT, reward-model fine-tuning, PPO-based RLHF) plus a Hybrid Engine unifying DeepSpeed training and inference optimizations for efficiency and scale.

title: OpenFlamingo: An Open-Source Framework for Training Large Autoregressive Vision-Language Models
summary: An open-source replication of Flamingo: a family of 3B-9B autoregressive vision-language models that insert cross-attention layers into frozen pretrained LLMs to attend to features from a frozen CLIP ViT vision encoder, trained on LAION-2B and Multimodal C4 and evaluated on seven vision-language benchmarks with in-context examples.

title: TOPIQ: A Top-down Approach from Semantics to Distortions for Image Quality Assessment
summary: Proposes TOPIQ/CFANet, a coarse-to-fine attention network for image quality assessment that propagates high-level semantic features top-down via cross-scale attention (CSA) and gated local pooling (GLP), achieving competitive FR/NR IQA with a ResNet50 backbone at ~13% FLOPS of prior best methods (per paper).

title: AgentBench: Evaluating LLMs as Agents
summary: AgentBench is a benchmark (not a model) that evaluates LLMs as agents across 8 interactive environments (OS, Database, Knowledge Graph, Digital Card Game, Lateral Thinking Puzzles, House-Holding, Web Shopping, Web Browsing), revealing a large gap between commercial API LLMs and open-source models, and identifying instruction following, long-term reasoning, and repetition-driven Task Limit Exceeded as key failure modes.

title: "Do Anything Now": Characterizing and Evaluating In-The-Wild Jailbreak Prompts on Large Language Models
summary: A measurement study (JAILBREAKHUB) collecting 1,405 in-the-wild jailbreak prompts, identifying 131 jailbreak communities via graph-based detection, and evaluating their attack success rates on six LLMs and three external safeguards. The paper proposes no new model architecture or training method; it is empirical security analysis.

title: Separate Anything You Describe
summary: AudioSep: a foundation model for open-domain language-queried audio source separation, combining a frozen CLAP text encoder (QueryNet) with a frequency-domain ResUNet (SeparationNet) conditioned via FiLM layers, trained on ~14,100 hours of multimodal data with waveform L1 loss, achieving strong zero-shot separation across many benchmarks.

title: OpenProteinSet: Training data for structural biology at scale
summary: The paper introduces OpenProteinSet, an open-source corpus of over 16 million precomputed protein multiple sequence alignments (MSAs), structural template hits, and AlphaFold2 structure predictions, and demonstrates its utility by retraining OpenFold (an AlphaFold2 reproduction) to near-parity with AlphaFold2 on CASP15.

title: AudioLDM 2: Learning Holistic Audio Generation with Self-supervised Pretraining
summary: A unified audio generation framework (speech, music, sound effects) that uses a self-supervised AudioMAE representation as a 'language of audio' (LOA), a GPT-2 model to translate conditions (text, phonemes, audio embeddings) into LOA, and a self-supervised pretrained latent diffusion model (Transformer-UNet over a VAE latent space) to generate audio from LOA.

title: Graph of Thoughts: Solving Elaborate Problems with Large Language Models
summary: GoT is a prompting framework (no model updates) that models LLM reasoning as an arbitrary directed graph of 'thoughts', enabling aggregation, refinement, and generation transformations beyond CoT/ToT, with a modular architecture (Prompter, Parser, Controller, GoO, GRS, scoring) and evaluation on sorting, set intersection, keyword counting, and document merging.

title: Dynamic 3D Gaussians: Tracking by Persistent Dynamic View Synthesis
summary: Extends 3D Gaussian Splatting to dynamic multi-view video by keeping Gaussian color/opacity/size persistent over time while optimizing per-timestep position and rotation, with local-rigidity, rotation-similarity, and isometry regularizers, so dense 6-DOF tracking emerges from differentiable rendering without correspondence inputs (Sections 1, 3).

title: A Survey on Large Language Model based Autonomous Agents
summary: A survey (not a model paper) that taxonomizes LLM-based autonomous agents around a unified four-module architecture (profiling, memory, planning, action), capability-acquisition strategies, applications, and evaluation methods. It proposes no trainable model, dataset, or experimental results of its own.

title: Nougat: Neural Optical Understanding for Academic Documents
summary: An end-to-end encoder-decoder transformer (Swin encoder + mBART-style decoder) that converts rasterized document page images into lightweight markup (with LaTeX math), trained on an automatically generated arXiv/PMC/IDL paired dataset (paraphrase of Sections 1-4).

title: EdgeMoE: Fast On-Device Inference of MoE-based Large Language Models
summary: EdgeMoE is an on-device inference engine for MoE LLMs that keeps non-expert weights in memory and expert weights on external storage, using expert-wise mixed-precision post-training quantization and statistical expert-activation prediction with preloading/pipelining and a frequency-plus-layer-index cache eviction policy to cut memory footprint and expert I/O latency.

title: Tracking Anything with Decoupled Video Segmentation
summary: DEVA decouples video segmentation into a task-specific image-level segmentation model plus a class-agnostic temporal propagation model (a modified XMem), combined via bi-directional propagation: in-clip consensus denoises image segmentations and merging fuses them with propagated masks (Sections 3.1-3.2).

title: ImageBind-LLM: Multi-modality Instruction Tuning
summary: ImageBind-LLM tunes LLaMA into a multi-modality instruction model by aligning ImageBind's image encoder with the LLM via a learnable bind network, injecting the transformed global feature into all word tokens of all transformer layers through an attention-free zero-initialized gate, and using a training-free visual cache model at inference to mitigate the training(image)-vs-inference(multi-modality) modality gap (per Sections 3.2.1-3.2.3).

title: Optimize Weight Rounding via Signed Gradient Descent for the Quantization of LLMs
summary: SignRound: a post-training weight-only quantization method that uses signed gradient descent (SignSGD) to jointly tune rounding values (V) and weight-clipping parameters (alpha, beta) via block-wise output reconstruction in ~200 steps, improving 2-4 bit weight-only quantization accuracy without extra inference overhead (paraphrase of Sections 1 and 3).

title: Efficient Memory Management for Large Language Model Serving with PagedAttention
summary: The paper proposes PagedAttention, an attention algorithm that stores KV caches in fixed-size non-contiguous blocks managed like OS virtual memory pages, and vLLM, a serving system with block-level KV cache management, copy-on-write sharing, preemption (swapping/recomputation), and iteration-level scheduling, achieving 2-4x throughput gains over FasterTransformer and Orca. This is a serving-systems contribution, not a new model architecture or tr

title: AudioSR: Versatile Audio Super-resolution at Scale
summary: A latent-diffusion-based audio super-resolution system that upsamples diverse audio (speech, music, sound effects) with flexible input bandwidth (2–16 kHz) to 24 kHz bandwidth at 48 kHz, using mel-spectrogram estimation plus a neural vocoder and low-frequency replacement post-processing (paraphrase of Sections 1–3).

title: Agents: An Open-source Framework for Autonomous Language Agents
summary: The paper presents AGENTS, an open-source Python library for building LLM-powered autonomous language agents with planning via symbolic SOPs, long-short term memory, tool usage, web navigation, multi-agent communication with dynamic scheduling, human-agent interaction, and automated SOP generation. It is a systems/framework paper, not a trainable neural architecture.

title: An Empirical Study of Scaling Instruct-Tuned Large Multimodal Models
summary: An empirical study (per the paper) scaling LLaVA-style visual instruction tuning from 13B to 33B/65B/70B LLMs, finding that larger LLM size, higher image resolution (336x336), and mixing language-only instruction data improve multimodal performance, and that LoRA/QLoRA tuning approaches full fine-tuning quality at lower cost.

title: FreeU: Free Lunch in Diffusion U-Net
summary: The paper shows that in diffusion U-Nets the backbone drives denoising while skip connections inject high-frequency features; at inference time only, re-weighting backbone features (structure-related scaling factor b) and attenuating low-frequency components of skip features (spectral modulation with factor s) improves sample quality with no training, parameters, memory, or sampling cost.

title: LongLoRA: Efficient Fine-tuning of Long-Context Large Language Models
summary: The paper proposes LongLoRA, a fine-tuning method that extends LLM context windows cheaply by (1) using shifted sparse attention (S2-Attn) only during training while keeping full attention at inference, and (2) an improved LoRA (LoRA+) that additionally trains embedding and normalization layers.

title: DeepSpeed-VisualChat: Multi-Round Multi-Image Interleave Chat via Multi-Modal Causal Attention
summary: A framework (per the paper) for multi-round, multi-image interleaved vision-language chat built on a MiniGPT4-style design: a frozen visual encoder, a trainable linear projection, a trainable/frozen LLM embedding, and a new parameter-free Multi-Modal Causal Attention (MMCA) that computes separate attention over image and text tokens, plus data blending to synthesize interleaved training data.

title: Vision Transformers Need Registers
summary: The paper shows that high-norm outlier tokens appear in feature maps of large, sufficiently trained vision transformers, that these tokens are recycled low-information patches storing global information, and that appending a few extra learnable 'register' tokens to the input sequence (discarded at output) removes the artifacts and improves dense prediction and object discovery (paraphrase of Sections 1-3).

title: Qwen Technical Report
summary: Qwen is a family of decoder-only LLMs (1.8B/7B/14B) pretrained on up to 3T multilingual tokens, aligned via SFT and RLHF, with specialized code and math variants. (Paper facts; not a Zerfoo implementation.)

title: DreamGaussian: Generative Gaussian Splatting for Efficient 3D Content Creation
summary: DreamGaussian adapts 3D Gaussian Splatting to optimization-based 3D generation (image-to-3D and text-to-3D) via SDS, with fast progressive densification, a mesh-extraction algorithm from Gaussians via block-wise local density queries, and a UV-space texture refinement stage using multi-step diffusion denoising with an MSE loss, producing textured meshes in ~2 minutes.

title: AutoAgents: A Framework for Automatic Agent Generation
summary: AutoAgents (paper fact) is an LLM orchestration framework that dynamically generates a team of specialized agents (Planner, Agent Observer, Plan Observer, Action Observer, custom agents) plus an execution plan in a Drafting Stage, then executes with self-refinement, collaborative refinement, and short/long/dynamic memory. It is a prompting/orchestration system over GPT-4, not a trainable neural architecture.

title: PixArt-α: Fast Training of Diffusion Transformer for Photorealistic Text-to-Image Synthesis
summary: PixArt-α is a DiT-based latent text-to-image diffusion model that reduces training cost via (1) three-stage training decomposition (pixel dependency, text-image alignment, aesthetics), (2) an efficient DiT variant with cross-attention for text conditioning and adaLN-single time conditioning with re-parameterization, and (3) high-information-density auto-labeled data (LLaVA captions on SAM).

title: Kandinsky: an Improved Text-to-Image Synthesis with Image Prior and Latent Diffusion
summary: A latent-diffusion text-to-image system (Kandinsky) that combines a separately trained image prior mapping CLIP text embeddings to CLIP image embeddings with a latent diffusion UNet and a modified MoVQ autoencoder, achieving FID 8.03 on COCO-30K at 256x256 (per Section 4/6).

title: Enhancing Financial Sentiment Analysis via Retrieval Augmented Large Language Models
summary: A framework combining instruction-tuned open-source LLMs (Llama-7B, ChatGLM2-6B) with a retrieval-augmented generation module that pulls context from financial news, research, and social media sources, improving financial sentiment classification accuracy and F1 by 15-48% over baselines.

title: SWE-bench: Can Language Models Resolve Real-World GitHub Issues?
summary: The paper introduces SWE-bench, an evaluation benchmark of 2,294 real GitHub issue tasks across 12 Python repositories where models generate patch files judged by fail-to-pass and pass-to-pass unit tests, plus SWE-bench-train (19,000 instances) and SWE-Llama 7b/13b, CodeLlama-Python models fine-tuned with LoRA on attention projections to emit gold patches. It is an evaluation framework and fine-tuning study, not a novel architecture.

title: Conceptual Framework for Autonomous Cognitive Entities
summary: The paper proposes ACE, a conceptual six-layer cognitive architecture for autonomous agents (Aspirational, Global Strategy, Agent Model, Executive Function, Cognitive Control, Task Prosecution) that uses LLMs as reasoning components with a natural-language constitution; it is a design framework, not an implemented or trained model.

title: Lag-Llama: Towards Foundation Models for Probabilistic Time Series Forecasting
summary: A decoder-only transformer foundation model for univariate probabilistic time series forecasting that uses lag features and date-time covariates as tokens, pretrained on a diverse 27-dataset corpus, showing strong zero-shot, fine-tuned, and few-shot adaptation performance (paraphrase of Sections 1, 4, 6).

title: Open X-Embodiment: Robotic Learning Datasets and RT-X Models
summary: The paper aggregates 60 robot datasets (1M+ trajectories, 22 embodiments) into the Open X-Embodiment repository and shows that Transformer-based policies (RT-1-X, RT-2-X) co-trained on this multi-robot mixture exhibit positive transfer, improving success rates over single-dataset baselines.

title: MiniGPT-v2: large language model as a unified interface for vision-language multi-task learning
summary: A vision-language model (frozen ViT encoder, token-concatenation, linear projection, LoRA-tuned LLaMA-2-chat 7B) trained with task-identifier tokens in a multi-task instruction template across three stages, achieving strong VQA and visual grounding results (paper claims).

title: NeMo Guardrails: A Toolkit for Controllable and Safe LLM Applications with Programmable Rails
summary: A runtime toolkit (not a model) that places a Colang-interpreting dialogue manager as a proxy between user and LLM, enforcing programmable topical rails (canonical forms + dialogue flows via three-step CoT prompting) and execution rails (fact-checking, hallucination, moderation) implemented as prompted LLM calls and Python actions.

title: A Survey on Video Diffusion Models
summary: A survey (not a model paper) that reviews video diffusion models across video generation, video editing, and video understanding, covering diffusion preliminaries (DDPM, SGM, Score SDE), datasets, evaluation metrics, and benchmark comparisons.

title: A decoder-only foundation model for time-series forecasting
summary: TimesFM: a ~200M-parameter decoder-only transformer with input patching, pretrained on ~O(100B) timepoints of real and synthetic time-series, achieving near-supervised zero-shot forecasting accuracy across unseen datasets (per Section 1 and Abstract).

title: Self-RAG: Learning to Retrieve, Generate, and Critique through Self-Reflection
summary: Self-RAG trains a single LM (7B/13B, Llama2-based) to adaptively decide when to retrieve passages and to emit special 'reflection tokens' (Retrieve, ISREL, ISSUP, ISUSE) that critique retrieved passages and its own generations, enabling controllable segment-level beam-search decoding at inference (Sections 1, 3).

title: Safe RLHF: Safe Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback
summary: The paper proposes Safe RLHF, which decouples human preference annotation into helpfulness and harmlessness, trains separate reward and cost models (the cost model combining pairwise Bradley-Terry loss with binary safety classification), and fine-tunes an LLM with PPO under a constrained (CMDP) objective solved via a Lagrangian multiplier that dynamically balances reward maximization against a cost constraint. Demonstrated on Alpaca-7B over three

title: AgentTuning: Enabling Generalized Agent Abilities for LLMs
summary: The paper proposes AgentTuning: building the AgentInstruct dataset (1,866 verified multi-turn agent interaction trajectories with ReAct-style CoT from six agent tasks) and a hybrid instruction-tuning method that mixes agent trajectories with general-domain instructions (mixture ratio η=0.2) to fine-tune Llama 2 chat models into AgentLM-7B/13B/70B, improving agent-task performance while preserving general NLP abilities.

title: Eureka: Human-Level Reward Design via Coding Large Language Models
summary: Eureka uses a coding LLM (GPT-4) with environment source code as context to zero-shot generate Python reward functions for RL tasks, then improves them via evolutionary search (batches of K=16 samples, 5 iterations, 5 restarts) and reward reflection (textual summaries of per-component reward statistics from PPO training), achieving human-level rewards on 29 IsaacGym environments and enabling gradient-free RLHF.

title: H2O Open Ecosystem for State-of-the-art Large Language Models
summary: The paper (per Section 1 and Abstract) presents h2oGPT and H2O LLM Studio: open-source tools for deploying, fine-tuning (LoRA/QLoRA, 4-bit, RLHF), evaluating, and serving large language models, plus a family of fine-tuned h2oGPT models. It is an ecosystem/tooling report, not a novel architecture paper.

title: SALMONN: Towards Generic Hearing Abilities for Large Language Models
summary: SALMONN is a multimodal LLM combining a Whisper speech encoder and a BEATs audio encoder via a window-level Q-Former into a Vicuna LLM with LoRA adaptors, trained in three stages (cross-modal pre-training, instruction tuning, and a proposed few-shot activation tuning) to gain generic hearing abilities and cross-modal emergent skills (per Sections 1, 3).

title: Wonder3D: Single Image to 3D using Cross-Domain Diffusion
summary: A cross-domain diffusion model fine-tuned from Stable Diffusion that jointly generates multi-view normal maps and color images from a single image (via a domain switcher and cross-domain/multi-view attention), followed by a geometry-aware SDF normal-fusion optimization to extract textured meshes.

title: Zero123++: a Single Image to Consistent Multi-view Diffusion Base Model
summary: A diffusion model finetuned from Stable Diffusion 2 (v-prediction) that tiles six novel views into one 3x2 image for multi-view consistency, using a linear noise schedule, scaled reference attention for local conditioning, and FlexDiffuse-style global image conditioning.

title: Inject Semantic Concepts into Image Tagging for Open-Set Recognition (RAM++)
summary: RAM++ is an open-set image tagging model that unifies individual tag supervision with global text supervision via a lightweight two-layer alignment decoder (ITTA), and uses LLM-generated tag descriptions with an automatic re-weighting module to enrich open-set visual concepts (Sections 3.1-3.3).

title: Zephyr: Direct Distillation of LM Alignment
summary: The paper aligns a 7B chat model (Zephyr-7B, based on Mistral-7B) entirely via distillation: distilled supervised fine-tuning (dSFT) on UltraChat, then distilled direct preference optimization (dDPO) on UltraFeedback AI-feedback preference pairs, requiring no human annotation and no online sampling, achieving state-of-the-art 7B chat benchmark results.

title: cuRobo: Parallelized Collision-Free Minimum-Jerk Robot Motion Generation
summary: Formulates collision-free manipulator motion generation as a global trajectory optimization problem and solves it via massively parallel GPU compute, combining L-BFGS with a novel parallel noisy line search, particle-based initialization, a parallel geometric planner, and differentiable kinematics/collision kernels to achieve ~50 ms planning (60× faster than SOTA CPU methods).

title: Does Role-Playing Chatbots Capture the Character Personalities? Assessing Personality Traits for Role-Playing Chatbots
summary: Proposes InCharacter, an interview-based framework that evaluates personality fidelity of role-playing agents (RPAs) by eliciting open-ended responses to psychologically derived questions and scoring them via LLM-based option conversion or expert rating, rather than relying on self-report scales.

title: LLM4Drive: A Survey of Large Language Models for Autonomous Driving
summary: A survey (not a model paper) that taxonomizes uses of (vision-)LLMs in autonomous driving across planning & control, perception, question answering, and generation, and catalogs datasets and benchmarks. It proposes no single architecture, training objective, or reproducible experiment.

title: AnyText: Multilingual Visual Text Generation And Editing
summary: A diffusion-based pipeline (built on ControlNet/Stable Diffusion) that renders accurate multilingual text in images via an auxiliary latent module (glyph, position, masked image) and a text embedding module (OCR-encoded glyph embeddings fused with caption embeddings), trained with text-control diffusion loss plus a text perceptual loss, along with the AnyWord-3M dataset and AnyText-benchmark.

title: S-LoRA: Serving Thousands of Concurrent LoRA Adapters
summary: A serving system (paper Sections 3-6) that scales multi-LoRA LLM inference via separated base/adapter batched computation, Unified Paging memory management, custom CUDA kernels for heterogeneous LoRA batching, and a low-overhead tensor parallelism strategy. It is a systems paper, not a new model architecture.

title: I2VGen-XL: High-Quality Image-to-Video Synthesis via Cascaded Diffusion Models
summary: A two-stage cascaded latent diffusion method for image-to-video synthesis: a base stage preserves input-image semantics/content via hierarchical encoders at low resolution, and a refinement stage denoises to 1280x720 with improved spatio-temporal detail (paraphrase of Sections 1-3).

title: mPLUG-Owl2: Revolutionizing Multi-modal Large Language Model with Modality Collaboration
summary: A multi-modal LLM (ViT-L/14 vision encoder + learnable-query visual abstractor + LLaMA-2-7B decoder) that adds a Modality-Adaptive Module (modality-separated layer norms and K/V projections with shared Q and FFN) so a single model improves both text-only and multi-modal tasks via two-stage training with a trainable vision encoder.

title: LongQLoRA: Efficient and Effective Method to Extend Context Length of Large Language Models
summary: The paper proposes LongQLoRA, which combines Position Interpolation, QLoRA (4-bit quantized base with LoRA adapters on all layers, rank 64), and LongLoRA's Shift Short Attention to extend LLaMA2 7B/13B context from 4096 to 8192 (even 12k) using a single 32GB V100, achieving perplexity on PG19/Proof-pile competitive with LongLoRA and near MPT-7B-8K, plus a 39k long-instruction dataset for Vicuna-13B.

title: GPT4All: An Ecosystem of Open Source Compressed Language Models
summary: A case study and technical overview of the GPT4All project: LLaMA/GPT-J-based instruction-tuned chatbots distilled from GPT-3.5-Turbo data, plus an ecosystem for distributing quantized open source LLMs on commodity hardware.

title: A Survey of Large Language Models in Medicine: Principles, Applications, and Challenges
summary: A survey (not a novel model) that taxonomizes medical LLM development into pre-training, fine-tuning (SFT/IFT/PEFT), and prompting (ICL/CoT/RAG), compares LLMs against task-specific lightweight models across medical tasks, and catalogs clinical applications and challenges. Paper facts only; no single architecture is proposed.

title: LCM-LoRA: A Universal Stable-Diffusion Acceleration Module
summary: The paper applies LoRA to Latent Consistency Distillation of Stable-Diffusion models (SD-V1.5, SSD-1B, SDXL), producing LCM-LoRA weights that act as a plug-in, training-free acceleration module: combined linearly with style LoRAs, they enable few-step text-to-image generation (Section 3).

title: Instruction-Following Evaluation for Large Language Models
summary: The paper introduces IFEval, a benchmark of ~541 prompts containing 25 types of 'verifiable instructions' (e.g., word counts, keyword frequency, JSON format) whose compliance can be checked by deterministic programs, plus strict and loose accuracy metrics for evaluating LLM instruction following (Sections 1-3).

title: Qwen-Audio: Advancing Universal Audio Understanding via Unified Large-Scale Audio-Language Models
summary: Qwen-Audio scales audio-language pre-training to 30+ tasks across speech, sound, and music using a Whisper-large-v2 audio encoder connected to Qwen-7B, with a hierarchical-tag multi-task format to avoid one-to-many label interference, plus SRWT word-level timestamp prediction; Qwen-Audio-Chat adds instruction-tuned multi-turn dialogue (per paper Sections 1, 3.1-3.3).

title: Video-LLaVA: Learning United Visual Representation by Alignment Before Projection
summary: Video-LLaVA pre-aligns image and video features into a unified visual feature space via LanguageBind encoders, then uses a shared projection layer to feed a single LLM (Vicuna-7B), enabling joint image+video training that mutually improves both modalities (paraphrase of Sections 1, 3).

title: Adapters: A Unified Library for Parameter-Efficient and Modular Transfer Learning
summary: The paper introduces the Adapters library, which unifies ten parameter-efficient fine-tuning methods (bottleneck adapters, LoRA, prefix tuning, (IA)3, Compacter, etc.) under one interface and adds composition blocks (Stack, Fuse, Split, BatchSplit, Parallel, Average) for modular transfer learning across 20 Transformer architectures (Sections 1, 3.3, 3.4).

title: Unmasking and Improving Data Credibility: A Study with Datasets for Training Harmless Language Models
summary: The paper introduces Docta, a training-free framework that estimates a label-noise transition matrix via k-NN label clusterability, scores and filters corrupted labels, and shows that cleaning safety-alignment datasets (Civil Comments, BeaverTails, SafeRLHF, Anthropic Harmless/Red-Team) improves downstream classification of BERT/GPT-2/Llama-2 fine-tunes. It is a data-cleaning methodology, not a new model architecture.

title: SuGaR: Surface-Aligned Gaussian Splatting for Efficient 3D Mesh Reconstruction and High-Quality Mesh Rendering
summary: SuGaR adds a regularization term to 3D Gaussian Splatting that aligns Gaussians with the scene surface, enabling fast mesh extraction via Poisson reconstruction on level-set samples, plus an optional joint refinement binding Gaussians to the mesh for editable, high-quality rendering.

title: LucidDreamer: Domain-free Generation of 3D Gaussian Splatting Scenes
summary: A training-free pipeline that alternates 'Dreaming' (Stable Diffusion inpainting guided by point-cloud projections plus monocular depth lifting) and 'Alignment' (depth-scale optimization and constrained point displacement) to build a unified point cloud, then optimizes 3D Gaussian splats for domain-free 3D scene generation from text, RGB, or RGBD inputs.

title: MEDITRON-70B: Scaling Medical Pretraining for Large Language Models
summary: The paper releases MEDITRON-7B/70B, Llama-2-based LLMs adapted to the medical domain via continued pretraining on a curated 48.1B-token corpus (PubMed papers/abstracts, clinical guidelines, 1% experience replay), plus supervised finetuning and CoT/self-consistency evaluation on medical QA benchmarks (paraphrase of Sections 1-6).

title: MagicAnimate: Temporally Consistent Human Image Animation using Diffusion Model
summary: A diffusion-based human image animation framework that inflates a 2D diffusion UNet with temporal attention, adds a trainable appearance encoder (a copy of the base UNet) whose features are concatenated into spatial self-attention for identity/background preservation, uses DensePose ControlNet for motion conditioning, image-video joint training, and sliding-window video fusion with averaged overlapping-frame noise predictions for long videos (par

title: Human Gaussian Splatting: Real-time Rendering of Animatable Avatars
summary: HuGS represents an animatable human avatar as canonical 3D Gaussian primitives deformed by forward Linear Blend Skinning with learned per-Gaussian skinning weights, refined by a small pose-dependent MLP for local non-rigid garment motion, enabling real-time novel-pose rendering from multi-view video.

title: Animate Anyone: Consistent and Controllable Image-to-Video Synthesis for Character Animation
summary: A pose-guided image-to-video diffusion framework (Animate Anyone) that animates a reference character image using a ReferenceNet with spatial attention, a lightweight pose guider, and temporal attention layers, trained in two stages on top of Stable Diffusion weights.

title: TaskWeaver: A Code-First Agent Framework
summary: TaskWeaver is a code-first LLM agent framework that converts user requests into executable Python, treats user-defined plugins as callable functions, and supports rich data structures, stateful execution, planning, self-reflection, and sandboxed code execution (Sections 1-5).

title: SyncTalk: The Devil is in the Synchronization for Talking Head Synthesis
summary: A NeRF-based speech-driven talking head synthesis method that improves synchronization of identity, lip motion, facial expressions, and head pose via a Face-Sync Controller (audio-visual encoder + 3D blendshape expression control), a Head-Sync Stabilizer (bundle adjustment over tracked keypoints), and a Portrait-Sync Generator for high-resolution detail restoration (per Sections 1 and 3).

title: Mamba: Linear-Time Sequence Modeling with Selective State Spaces
summary: The paper introduces selective state space models (S6): SSM parameters (Delta, B, C) become input-dependent, removing linear time invariance, plus a hardware-aware fused scan algorithm, and a simplified homogeneous Mamba block (no attention or MLP blocks) that matches Transformer quality on language, DNA, and audio at linear scaling in sequence length.

title: Sequential Modeling Enables Scalable Learning for Large Vision Models
summary: The paper trains Large Vision Models (LVMs) purely on pixels: images/videos/annotations are formatted as 'visual sentences', tokenized per-image by a VQGAN (256 tokens, codebook 8192), and a LLaMA-style causal transformer (up to 3B parameters) is trained with next-token cross-entropy on 420B tokens (UVDv1, 1.64B images), enabling task specification via visual prompting at test time.

title: OpenVoice: Versatile Instant Voice Cloning
summary: OpenVoice decouples instant voice cloning into a base speaker TTS model (controlling language and styles like emotion, accent, rhythm, pauses, intonation) and a tone color converter (encoder, invertible normalizing flow conditioned on speaker embeddings, HiFi-GAN decoder), enabling zero-shot cross-lingual cloning and fast feed-forward inference (paper Sections 1-2).

title: Magicoder: Source Code Is All You Need
summary: Proposes OSS-Instruct, a method where a teacher LLM generates diverse code instruction-tuning data (problem-solution pairs) inspired by random open-source seed code snippets; finetuning CodeLlama-Python-7B and DeepSeek-Coder-6.7B on 75K such samples (Magicoder) and then on Evol-Instruct data (MagicoderS) yields large code-generation gains.

title: SplaTAM: Splat, Track & Map 3D Gaussians for Dense RGB-D SLAM
summary: A dense RGB-D SLAM system that represents the scene as isotropic, view-independent 3D Gaussians optimized online via differentiable splatting, jointly estimating camera poses (tracking) and a Gaussian map (densification + update), achieving state-of-the-art pose accuracy and rendering quality (paper, Sections 1, 3, 5).

title: A Task is Worth One Word: Learning with Task Prompts for High-Quality Versatile Image Inpainting
summary: PowerPaint fine-tunes Stable Diffusion for image inpainting using learnable task prompts (Pobj, Pctxt, Pshape) with task-specific training strategies, enabling text-guided object inpainting, context-aware filling, object removal via negative prompting, and shape-guided inpainting via prompt interpolation within one model.

title: MotionCtrl: A Unified and Flexible Motion Controller for Video Generation
summary: MotionCtrl adds two adapter-like modules to a pretrained latent video diffusion model (LVDM/VideoCrafter1): a Camera Motion Control Module (CMCM) that injects camera pose sequences into temporal transformers, and an Object Motion Control Module (OMCM) that injects trajectory features into U-Net convolutional layers, enabling independent or joint camera/object motion control via a multi-step training strategy (paper Sections 1, 3.2).

title: Generative agent-based modeling with actions grounded in physical, social, or digital space using Concordia
summary: Concordia is a library for Generative Agent-Based Models (GABMs): LLM-driven agents with modular components and associative memory interact in language-mediated simulations, with a Game Master (GM) agent that grounds actions, maintains world state and grounded variables, and can integrate digital apps/APIs. It is a system/framework paper, not a trainable neural architecture.

title: MatterGen: a generative model for inorganic materials design
summary: MatterGen is a diffusion-based generative model that produces stable inorganic crystal structures by jointly denoising atom types, fractional coordinates, and the periodic lattice, and can be fine-tuned via adapter modules with classifier-free guidance to steer generation toward chemistry, symmetry, and scalar property constraints (paraphrase of Sections 1-2 and Appendices A-B).

title: Pearl: A Production-ready Reinforcement Learning Agent
summary: Pearl is a modular PyTorch RL library unifying policy learners (DQN variants, SAC, PPO, offline RL), intelligent exploration, safety modules, history summarization, and dynamic action spaces in one agent framework (Sections 1-2).

title: PhotoMaker: Customizing Realistic Human Photos via Stacked ID Embedding
summary: PhotoMaker is a tuning-free personalized text-to-image method built on SDXL that encodes an arbitrary number of ID images into a stacked ID embedding (fused with the class-word text embedding via two MLPs and concatenated along the length dimension), which replaces the class-word position in the text embedding and is merged by the diffusion model's cross-attention, plus an ID-oriented data construction pipeline (Sec. 3.2-3.3).

title: An LLM Compiler for Parallel Function Calling
summary: LLMCompiler is an orchestration framework (not a new neural architecture) that decomposes user queries into a DAG of function-calling tasks via a Planner LLM, dispatches them with a Task Fetching Unit, executes them in parallel with an Executor, and supports dynamic replanning, yielding latency/cost/accuracy gains over ReAct.

title: Vary: Scaling up the Vision Vocabulary for Large Vision-Language Models
summary: Proposes Vary, a two-stage method for LVLMs: (1) train a new vision vocabulary network (SAM ViTDet-based encoder plus conv token mergers) with a tiny decoder-only LLM via autoregression on document/chart data, then (2) fuse this frozen new vocabulary in parallel with frozen CLIP-ViT, training only projection linears and the 7B LLM, enabling dense OCR, document/chart parsing while retaining general abilities.

title: EasyVolcap: Accelerating Neural Volumetric Video Research
summary: A Python/PyTorch library unifying multi-view video data processing, 4D neural scene reconstruction (feature embedding + MLP regressors), and dynamic volumetric video rendering, with a native viewer and configuration system.

title: Upscale-A-Video: Temporal-Consistent Diffusion Model for Real-World Video Super-Resolution
summary: A text-guided latent diffusion framework for real-world video super-resolution that fine-tunes a pretrained SD x4 upscaler with temporal layers (3D convs, temporal attention) in the U-Net and VAE-Decoder for local consistency, plus a training-free flow-guided recurrent latent propagation module for global consistency, with text-prompt and noise-level controls balancing fidelity and quality (paper facts).

title: Gaussian Splatting SLAM
summary: First real-time monocular/RGB-D SLAM system using 3D Gaussian Splatting as the sole scene representation, with direct camera-pose optimisation via an analytic SE(3) Jacobian, isotropic shape regularisation, and visibility-based Gaussian insertion/pruning (paraphrase of Sections 1, 3).

title: VILA: On Pre-training for Visual Language Models
summary: The paper studies pre-training design choices for auto-regressive visual language models (VLMs), finding that (1) fine-tuning the LLM (not freezing it) during pre-training is essential for in-context learning, (2) interleaved image-text corpora (e.g., MMC4) outperform image-text pairs and preserve text-only ability, and (3) re-blending text-only instruction data into SFT recovers text degradation and boosts VLM accuracy. It builds the VILA model

title: PromptBench: A Unified Library for Evaluation of Large Language Models
summary: PromptBench is a modular Python library for evaluating LLMs: prompt construction/engineering, dataset and model loading, adversarial prompt attacks, dynamic/semantic evaluation protocols, and analysis tools (paper Sections 1-2). It is an evaluation framework, not a trainable neural architecture.

title: FoundationPose: Unified 6D Pose Estimation and Tracking of Novel Objects
summary: A unified RGBD foundation model that estimates and tracks 6D pose of novel objects without fine-tuning, in both model-based (CAD given) and model-free (few reference images) setups, using LLM-aided synthetic data, an SDF-based neural object field for novel-view RGBD rendering, a transformer-based pose refinement network, and a hierarchical pose ranking network trained with a pose-conditioned triplet loss (per Secs. 3.1-3.4).

title: TigerBot: An Open Multilingual Multitask LLM
summary: The TigerBot family (7B–180B base and chat LLMs) built by continual pretraining from Llama-2/BLOOM with a curated multilingual data mix, expanded tokenizer, holistic training, SFT, rejection-sampling and DPO alignment, plus long-context, quantization, safety, and application tooling (per paper Sections 1–3).

title: CogAgent: A Visual Language Model for GUI Agents
summary: CogAgent is an 18B-parameter visual language model built on CogVLM that adds a lightweight high-resolution cross-module (cross-attention at hidden size 1024 fed by a 0.30B EVA2-CLIP-L encoder on 1120x1120 inputs) so GUI screenshots with tiny text/icons can be understood efficiently, achieving SOTA on VQA and GUI navigation benchmarks (Mind2Web, AITW).

title: DreamTalk: When Expressive Talking Head Generation Meets Diffusion Probabilistic Models
summary: A diffusion-based framework (DreamTalk) for audio-driven emotional talking head generation, combining a transformer denoising network over 3DMM face motions, a style-aware lip expert for lip-sync guidance, and a diffusion-based style predictor that infers speaking style from audio plus portrait, with classifier-free guidance for style intensity control (per Section III).

title: Amphion: An Open-Source Audio, Music and Speech Generation Toolkit
summary: Amphion is an open-source toolkit unifying audio, music, and speech generation tasks (TTS, TTA, SVC, vocoders, codecs) with shared data processing, training pipelines, pre-trained models, and evaluation metrics.

title: Point Transformer V3: Simpler, Faster, Stronger
summary: PTv3 is a 3D point cloud transformer that trades precise KNN neighborhoods and relative positional encoding for space-filling-curve serialization, patch attention, and grid pooling, enabling a large receptive field (up to 1024 points), ~3.3x faster inference and ~10x lower memory than PTv2, with state-of-the-art results on 20+ 3D perception tasks.

title: SkySense: A Multi-Modal Remote Sensing Foundation Model Towards Universal Interpretation for Earth Observation Imagery
summary: A 2.06B-parameter multi-modal remote sensing foundation model with a factorized spatiotemporal encoder (Swin-H for high-res optical, ViT-L for multispectral and SAR), pre-trained via Multi-Granularity Contrastive Learning, Cross-Modal Alignment, and Geo-Context Prototype Learning on 21.5M aligned temporal sequences, achieving SOTA across 16 datasets and 7 tasks.

title: StarVector: Generating Scalable Vector Graphics Code from Images
summary: StarVector is a multimodal LLM (ViT/SigLIP image encoder + non-linear adapter + StarCoder/StarCoder2 decoder LLM) that generates SVG code autoregressively from images or text, trained on the 2M-sample SVG-Stack dataset and evaluated on SVG-Bench with a DinoScore perceptual metric (paraphrase of Sections 1, 4).

title: PowerInfer: Fast Large Language Model Serving with a Consumer-grade GPU
summary: PowerInfer is a GPU-CPU hybrid LLM inference engine that exploits power-law neuron activation locality: hot neurons are preloaded on GPU, cold neurons computed on CPU, with adaptive activation predictors and neuron-aware sparse operators, achieving up to 11.69x speedup over llama.cpp on a consumer GPU (paper facts).

title: StreamDiffusion: A Pipeline-level Solution for Real-time Interactive Generation
summary: A pipeline-level system (not a new model) that makes diffusion-based image-to-image generation real-time by batching staggered denoising steps (Stream Batch), approximating classifier-free guidance with virtual residual noise (R-CFG), and probabilistically skipping computation for static inputs (SSF), plus engineering accelerations (IO queues, caching, TensorRT, tiny VAE).

title: Generative Multimodal Models are In-Context Learners
summary: Emu2 (37B) is a generative multimodal model trained with a unified predict-the-next-element autoregressive objective over interleaved text, image, and video embeddings, demonstrating strong multimodal in-context learning and, after instruction tuning, state-of-the-art multimodal understanding and controllable visual generation.

title: DUSt3R: Geometric 3D Vision Made Easy
summary: DUSt3R regresses dense pointmaps (per-pixel 3D points) from uncalibrated, unposed image pairs using a Siamese ViT encoder with cross-attention transformer decoders, trained with a confidence-weighted 3D regression loss, plus a global alignment optimization for multi-view reconstruction (paraphrase of Sections 1, 3).

title: Fast Inference of Mixture-of-Experts Language Models with Offloading
summary: The paper proposes MoE-specific inference offloading for Mixtral-8x7B: an LRU cache of active experts on GPU plus speculative expert prefetching (guessing next-layer experts from current hidden states), combined with mixed HQQ quantization (attention at 4/16-bit, experts at 2-3 bit), enabling 2-3 tokens/sec interactive generation on consumer GPUs.

title: Video Understanding with Large Language Models: A Survey
summary: A survey (not a model paper) that taxonomizes Vid-LLMs into Video Analyzer × LLM, Video Embedder × LLM, and (Analyzer + Embedder) × LLM, with five LLM functional roles (Summarizer, Manager, Text Decoder, Regressor, Hidden Layer), and reviews tasks, datasets, benchmarks, training strategies, and future directions.

title: Moonshot: Towards Controllable Video Generation and Editing with Multimodal Conditions
summary: MoonShot is a latent video diffusion model conditioned on both text and image via a Multimodal Video Block (MVB) with decoupled text/image cross-attention, enabling zero-shot subject-customized video generation, image animation, video editing, and optional direct reuse of pre-trained image ControlNets without extra training (Sections 1, 3).

title: From Audio to Photoreal Embodiment: Synthesizing Humans in Conversations
summary: A framework that converts dyadic conversational audio into full-body photoreal avatar motion by combining a VQ-Transformer that samples diverse coarse guide poses with diffusion models that infill high-frequency face and body motion, plus a new multi-view conversational dataset with photorealistic reconstructions.

title: Mobile ALOHA: Learning Bimanual Mobile Manipulation with Low-Cost Whole-Body Teleoperation
summary: A low-cost hardware system (ALOHA arms on a wheeled base) for whole-body teleoperation, plus a co-training recipe showing that mixing static ALOHA data with 20-50 mobile demonstrations enables behavior cloning of bimanual mobile manipulation tasks (paper facts, Sections 1, 3, 4).

title: TinyLlama: An Open-Source Small Language Model
summary: A 1.1B-parameter Llama 2-style decoder-only Transformer pretrained on ~3 trillion tokens (v1.0) and retrained as v1.1 with a three-stage pipeline (basic pretraining, domain-specific continual pretraining, cooldown via enlarged batch size), outperforming similarly sized open models on commonsense and problem-solving benchmarks.

title: DeepSeek LLM: Scaling Open-Source Language Models with Longtermism
summary: The paper studies scaling laws for LLMs (batch size, learning rate, and model/data allocation using non-embedding FLOPs/token), then trains open-source 7B and 67B decoder-only LLMs (LLaMA-style with RMSNorm, SwiGLU, RoPE, GQA for 67B, multi-step LR scheduler) on 2T tokens, followed by SFT and DPO to create chat models that outperform LLaMA-2 70B on many benchmarks.

title: DeepSeekMoE: Towards Ultimate Expert Specialization in Mixture-of-Experts Language Models
summary: Proposes DeepSeekMoE, a MoE Transformer LM architecture with fine-grained expert segmentation (splitting FFN experts into m smaller ones and activating mK) and shared expert isolation (always-on shared experts), plus expert/device-level balance losses, showing better expert specialization than GShard at 2B/16B/145B scales.

title: VMamba: Visual State Space Model
summary: The paper adapts the Mamba selective state-space model into a vision backbone (VMamba) built from Visual State-Space (VSS) blocks, introducing 2D-Selective-Scan (SS2D) that unfolds image patches along four 1D traversal paths (Cross-Scan), processes each with an S6 block, and merges results (Cross-Merge), achieving linear-complexity visual representation learning (per Section 4).

title: Medusa: Simple LLM Inference Acceleration Framework with Multiple Decoding Heads
summary: Medusa adds K extra decoding heads on top of a frozen or jointly fine-tuned LLM's last hidden states to predict multiple future tokens in parallel, uses tree attention to verify candidate continuations in one pass, and introduces typical acceptance and self-distillation, achieving 2.2-2.8x decoding speedup (paper claims).

title: Depth Anything: Unleashing the Power of Large-Scale Unlabeled Data
summary: A monocular depth estimation foundation model trained via self-training on 1.5M labeled and ~62M pseudo-labeled unlabeled images, using strong perturbations (color jitter, Gaussian blur, CutMix) on unlabeled data and a tolerance-margin feature alignment loss to a frozen DINOv2 encoder, achieving strong zero-shot relative depth and downstream metric depth/segmentation transfer.

title: Scalable High-Resolution Pixel-Space Image Synthesis with Hourglass Diffusion Transformers
summary: HDiT is a hierarchical pure-transformer diffusion backbone that processes images directly in pixel space, using an hourglass structure with global attention only at low resolutions and neighborhood (local) attention at higher resolutions, achieving O(n) compute scaling with pixel count and state-of-the-art pixel-space diffusion results on FFHQ-1024 and competitive results on ImageNet-256.

title: DeepSeek-Coder: When the Large Language Model Meets Programming -- The Rise of Code Intelligence
summary: A family of open-source decoder-only code LLMs (1.3B/6.7B/33B) trained from scratch on 2T tokens of 87-language, repository-level organized code, using next-token prediction plus 50% PSM fill-in-the-middle, 16K context, and instruction tuning, achieving state-of-the-art open-source code benchmark results.

title: YOLO-World: Real-Time Open-Vocabulary Object Detection
summary: The paper proposes YOLO-World, a YOLOv8-based open-vocabulary detector that fuses CLIP text embeddings with image features via a Re-parameterizable Vision-Language PAN (RepVL-PAN), trained with region-text contrastive pre-training on detection, grounding, and pseudo-labeled image-text data, achieving 35.4 AP zero-shot on LVIS at 52.0 FPS (paper-reported).

title: RAPTOR: Recursive Abstractive Processing for Tree-Organized Retrieval
summary: RAPTOR (Section 3) recursively embeds, clusters (GMM with UMAP + BIC), and summarizes text chunks to build a tree, then retrieves from all layers via a 'collapsed tree' cosine-similarity search, improving QA over flat chunk retrieval.

title: Executable Code Actions Elicit Better LLM Agents
summary: Proposes CodeAct, a framework where LLM agents emit executable Python code as a unified action space, shows it outperforms JSON/text action formats (up to 20% higher success rate on a new M3 ToolEval benchmark), and releases CodeActInstruct (7k multi-turn trajectories) plus CodeActAgent models fine-tuned from LLaMA-2 and Mistral-7B.

title: OpenMoE: An Early Effort on Open Mixture-of-Experts Language Models
summary: Releases fully open decoder-only ST-MoE-style LLMs (650M–34B params, up to ~1.1T tokens) and analyzes MoE routing, finding Context-Independent Specialization, Early Routing Learning, and Drop-towards-the-End token dropping, plus design recommendations for future MoE training.

title: DeepSeekMath: Pushing the Limits of Mathematical Reasoning in Open Language Models
summary: The paper introduces DeepSeekMath 7B, a 7B-parameter language model for mathematical reasoning created by continued pretraining of DeepSeek-Coder-Base-v1.5 7B on a 120B-token math corpus mined from Common Crawl with an iterative fastText classifier pipeline, plus instruction tuning and a new critic-free RL algorithm (GRPO) that lifts MATH accuracy to 51.7%.

title: EVA-CLIP-18B: Scaling CLIP to 18 Billion Parameters
summary: The paper scales contrastive language-image pretraining (CLIP) to an 18.1B-parameter model (EVA-CLIP-18B) using an EVA-style weak-to-strong recipe: a large EVA vision transformer is distilled from a smaller EVA-CLIP teacher, then used to initialize the vision encoder for CLIP contrastive pretraining on a fixed ~2B image-text dataset, achieving 80.7% average zero-shot top-1 accuracy across 27 image classification benchmarks (paper-reported).

title: LGM: Large Multi-View Gaussian Model for High-Resolution 3D Content Creation
summary: LGM (per the paper) is a feed-forward framework that generates high-resolution 3D Gaussians from text or single-view images: a multi-view diffusion model (MVDream/ImageDream) synthesizes four views, and an asymmetric U-Net with cross-view self-attention predicts per-pixel 3D Gaussian parameters that are fused and supervised via differentiable Gaussian splatting rendering, with an optional Gaussian-to-mesh conversion pipeline.

title: SPHINX-X: Scaling Data and Parameters for a Family of Multi-modal Large Language Models
summary: The paper (Sections 1, 3) presents SPHINX-X, a family of multimodal LLMs built on SPHINX with three modifications: reducing four vision encoders to two (DINOv2 + CLIP-ConvNeXt, 'Mixture of Visual experts'), replacing fully-padded sub-images with a learnable skip token, and collapsing multi-stage training into one-stage all-in-one training over a large multi-domain dataset, using base LLMs from TinyLlama-1.1B to Mixtral-8x7B.

title: OS-Copilot: Towards Generalist Computer Agents with Self-Improvement
summary: OS-Copilot is a prompting-based framework for OS-level LLM agents with a planner, memory-based configurator, and actor (executor/critic/refiner); FRIDAY, built on it, self-improves by generating and retaining Python tools via self-directed learning, improving GAIA and spreadsheet-task success.

title: World Model on Million-Length Video And Language With RingAttention
summary: The paper (LWM) details the full pipeline for building 7B Llama2-based autoregressive transformers with 1M-token context via Blockwise RingAttention, progressive context extension (32K→1M) with scaled RoPE θ, model-generated QA data for long-context chat, and a second stage adding VQGAN-tokenized image/video modalities with masked sequence packing and loss re-weighting.

title: Mixtures of Experts Unlock Parameter Scaling for Deep RL
summary: The paper shows that replacing the penultimate dense layer of value-based deep RL agents (DQN, Rainbow) with Soft Mixture-of-Experts modules makes performance scale positively with parameter count, unlike naively widened baselines (paper Sections 1, 4.1).

title: Automated Unit Test Improvement using Large Language Models at Meta
summary: TestGen-LLM: an LLM-agnostic 'Assured Offline LLMSE' pipeline at Meta that extends existing Kotlin unit test classes with LLM-generated test cases, filtered by build, reliable-pass (5 runs), and coverage-improvement checks so only verifiably improved tests are recommended for human review.

title: How NeRFs and 3D Gaussian Splatting are Reshaping SLAM: a Survey
summary: A survey (not a model paper) reviewing 80 SLAM systems built on NeRF and 3D Gaussian Splatting representations, with a taxonomy by sensor type (RGB-D, RGB, LiDAR), datasets, metrics, and analysis of limitations such as real-time constraints and catastrophic forgetting.

title: OpenCodeInterpreter: Integrating Code Generation with Execution and Refinement
summary: The paper introduces OpenCodeInterpreter, a family of open-source code LLMs fine-tuned on CodeFeedback, a 68K multi-turn instruction dataset combining execution feedback (compiler/runtime diagnostics) and simulated human feedback, enabling iterative generate-execute-refine code generation that approaches GPT-4 Code Interpreter performance on HumanEval/MBPP (Section 1, Section 2, Section 4).

title: MobileLLM: Optimizing Sub-billion Parameter Language Models for On-Device Use Cases
summary: The paper shows that for sub-billion parameter LLMs, architecture matters: deep-and-thin transformers with SwiGLU FFNs, input-output embedding sharing, grouped-query attention, and immediate block-wise weight sharing (MobileLLM-LS) outperform prior same-size models on zero-shot reasoning, chat, and API-calling tasks.

title: FlexLLM: A System for Co-Serving Large Language Model Inference and Parameter-Efficient Finetuning
summary: FlexLLM is a GPU serving system (not a model) that co-serves LLM inference and PEFT finetuning on shared GPUs via token-level computation fusion, dependent parallelization, graph pruning, and a hybrid token scheduler, maintaining inference SLOs while improving finetuning throughput.

title: OOTDiffusion: Outfitting Fusion based Latent Diffusion for Controllable Virtual Try-on
summary: An LDM-based virtual try-on method that adds an outfitting UNet to learn garment latent features in one step, fuses them into the denoising UNet's self-attention layers via spatial concatenation (outfitting fusion), and uses outfitting dropout during training to enable classifier-free guidance over garment strength.

title: TripoSR: Fast 3D Object Reconstruction from a Single Image
summary: A feed-forward transformer-based model (built on LRM) that reconstructs a textured 3D mesh from a single RGB image in under 0.5 seconds on an A100, using a DINOv1 image encoder, an image-to-triplane transformer decoder, and a triplane NeRF with rendering-based supervision (per Sections 2.1-2.3).

title: GaLore: Memory-Efficient LLM Training by Gradient Low-Rank Projection
summary: GaLore is a training strategy (not an architecture) that projects weight gradients onto a slowly-changing low-rank subspace via SVD-derived projectors P and Q, so Adam-style optimizer states are stored in the r-dimensional projected space instead of full m×n, cutting optimizer memory substantially while keeping full-rank weights (Sections 3.3, 4.2).

title: Yi: Open Foundation Models by 01.AI
summary: The Yi paper (Sections 1-2) introduces 6B/34B decoder-only Transformer language models pretrained on 3.1T filtered bilingual tokens, using a LLaMA-style architecture with Grouped-Query Attention, SwiGLU activation, and RoPE with adjusted base frequency, plus chat finetuning on <10K curated instructions, 200K context extension, vision-language extension, and depth upscaling.

title: Divide and Conquer: High-Resolution Industrial Anomaly Detection via Memory Efficient Tiled Ensemble
summary: A model-agnostic tiled ensemble method for industrial anomaly detection: high-resolution images are split into (possibly overlapping) tiles, a dedicated anomaly-detection model is trained per tile location, and tile predictions are merged (pixel-wise averaging, score averaging, seam smoothing) so GPU memory stays at single-tile levels while enabling small-anomaly detection.

title: DeepSeek-VL: Towards Real-World Vision-Language Understanding
summary: An open-source vision-language model family (1.3B/7B) combining a hybrid vision encoder (SigLIP-L at 384x384 plus SAM-B at 1024x1024), a two-layer hybrid MLP adaptor, and a DeepSeek LLM, trained in three stages with joint language-multimodal pretraining (70:30 language:multimodal ratio) and modality warm-up to preserve language ability.

title: FaceChain-SuDe: Building Derived Class to Inherit Category Attributes for One-shot Subject-Driven Generation
summary: Proposes SuDe, a plug-and-play regularization for one-shot subject-driven text-to-image generation: subject-generated images are constrained to be classifiable into the subject's semantic category via the diffusion model's implicit classifier, so the subject inherits category 'public attributes' while learning 'private attributes' from one example image.

title: BrushNet: A Plug-and-Play Image Inpainting Model with Decomposed Dual-Branch Diffusion
summary: BrushNet (per Sec. 4) adds a trainable dual branch that extracts pixel-level masked-image features (from a VAE-encoded masked image, noisy latent, and downsampled mask, with cross-attention removed) and inserts them layer-by-layer via zero convolutions into a frozen pre-trained diffusion UNet, plus a blurred-mask pixel-space blending step for unmasked-region preservation.

title: AutoDev: Automated AI-Driven Development
summary: AutoDev is an agentic framework (not a new model) in which LLM-driven AI agents autonomously plan and execute software engineering tasks by issuing commands (file editing, retrieval, build, test, git) inside a Docker-based Evaluation Environment, coordinated by a Conversation Manager and Agent Scheduler. Evaluated on HumanEval with GPT-4, achieving 91.5% Pass@1 for code generation and 87.8% for test generation.

title: Simple and Scalable Strategies to Continually Pre-train Large Language Models
summary: The paper shows empirically that continual pre-training of decoder-only transformer LLMs (405M and 10B parameters) using learning-rate re-warming, LR re-decaying, and compute-equivalent replay of previous data matches the final loss and average LM-evaluation performance of full re-training on the union of datasets, at a fraction of the compute, for weak (English→English) and strong (English→German) distribution shifts; it also proposes infinite l

title: RAFT: Adapting Language Model to Domain Specific RAG
summary: RAFT is a fine-tuning recipe (not a new architecture) that adapts pretrained LLMs for domain-specific RAG by training on question + golden/distractor document mixtures with chain-of-thought answers containing verbatim citations, improving robustness to imperfect retrieval (Sections 1, 3).

title: FeatUp: A Model-Agnostic Framework for Features at Any Resolution
summary: FeatUp restores spatial resolution in deep vision features via multi-view consistency: a learned upsampler (either a stack of Joint Bilateral Upsamplers or a per-image implicit MLP) is trained so a learned downsampler of the high-resolution features reproduces low-resolution features from jittered image views (paper, Sections 1, 3).

title: One-Step Image Translation with Text-to-Image Models
summary: The paper adapts a pre-trained one-step latent diffusion model (SD-Turbo) into an image-to-image translation generator (CycleGAN-Turbo for unpaired, pix2pix-Turbo for paired settings) by feeding the conditioning image directly into the U-Net noise branch, adding LoRA adapters, first-stage encoder-decoder skip connections via zero-conv, and training with adversarial plus cycle-consistency/identity losses.

title: mPLUG-DocOwl 1.5: Unified Structure Learning for OCR-free Document Understanding
summary: Proposes Unified Structure Learning (structure-aware parsing plus multi-grained text localization across 5 domains), an H-Reducer vision-to-text module (1x4 convolution merging horizontal visual features followed by a fully connected layer), the DocStruct4M training set, DocReason25K reasoning data, and a two-stage training framework, achieving SOTA OCR-free performance on 10 document understanding benchmarks (paper-reported).

title: LLMLingua-2: Data Distillation for Efficient and Faithful Task-Agnostic Prompt Compression
summary: Formulates task-agnostic prompt compression as binary token classification (preserve/discard) using a Transformer encoder trained on a GPT-4-distilled extractive compression dataset built from MeetingBank, yielding small, fast, faithful compressors (XLM-RoBERTa-large or mBERT based).

title: Mora: Enabling Generalist Video Generation via A Multi-Agent Framework
summary: Mora is a multi-agent framework that chains open-source LLM, text-to-image, image-to-image, image-to-video, and video-connection models to replicate Sora-like video generation, with self-modulated multi-agent fine-tuning, data-free training-data synthesis, and human-in-the-loop MLLM data filtering (Sections 1, 3.1, 3.2).

title: LlamaFactory: Unified Efficient Fine-Tuning of 100+ Language Models
summary: A modular framework (Model Loader, Data Worker, Trainer) that unifies efficient fine-tuning methods (LoRA, QLoRA, GaLore, BAdam, etc.) and training approaches (pre-training, SFT, RLHF, DPO) across 100+ LLMs, with a no-code web UI (LlamaBoard).

title: StreamingT2V: Consistent, Dynamic, and Extendable Long Video Generation from Text
summary: An autoregressive text-to-long-video framework that extends a pre-trained text-to-video diffusion model with a short-term memory block (CAM), a long-term memory block (APM), and a randomized blending scheme for autoregressive video enhancement, producing temporally consistent videos of 240-1200+ frames (per paper Sections 1, 4).

title: LLM Agent Operating System
summary: AIOS is a systems architecture (not a model) that isolates LLM-based agent applications from resources via an AIOS kernel providing scheduling, context/memory/storage/tool management, and access control, with an SDK; it reports up to 2.1x faster agent execution (Section 1, Abstract).

title: VoiceCraft: Zero-Shot Speech Editing and Text-to-Speech in the Wild
summary: A Transformer-based neural codec language model (NCLM) that performs token infilling over Encodec RVQ tokens via a two-step token rearrangement (causal masking + delayed stacking), achieving state-of-the-art speech editing and zero-shot TTS on in-the-wild data, plus the RealEdit evaluation dataset (per Sections 1, 3, 4).

title: AniPortrait: Audio-Driven Synthesis of Photorealistic Portrait Animation
summary: A two-stage framework (per the paper): Audio2Lmk extracts 3D facial mesh and head pose from audio via wav2vec 2.0 features and projects them to 2D landmarks; Lmk2Video uses a Stable Diffusion 1.5 backbone with ReferenceNet, a multi-scale ControlNet-style PoseGuider, and a temporal motion module to render photorealistic talking-portrait video from landmarks and a reference image.

title: 2D Gaussian Splatting for Geometrically Accurate Radiance Fields
summary: The paper proposes 2D Gaussian Splatting (2DGS), representing a radiance field as a set of 2D oriented planar Gaussian disks instead of 3D Gaussians, rendered via perspective-correct ray-splat intersection and alpha blending, with depth-distortion and normal-consistency regularizers enabling accurate surface reconstruction and mesh extraction from multi-view RGB images.

title: Mini-Gemini: Mining the Potential of Multi-modality Vision Language Models
summary: A VLM framework (per Sections 3.1-3.3) using dual vision encoders (CLIP ViT for low-resolution embeddings, ConvNeXt for high-resolution candidates), a patch info mining cross-attention module that enriches visual tokens without increasing their count, an LLM for text/image understanding, and text-prompt-driven SDXL image generation, trained with a two-stage recipe on ~1.2M caption pairs and ~1.5M instruction conversations.

title: TFB: Towards Comprehensive and Fair Benchmarking of Time Series Forecasting Methods
summary: TFB is a benchmarking framework (not a model) for time series forecasting: it contributes datasets from 10 domains with a six-characteristic taxonomy (trend, seasonality, stationarity, shifting, transition, correlation), a unified pipeline covering statistical/ML/DL methods, fixed and rolling evaluation strategies, eight error metrics, and findings such as VAR/LR beating SOTA deep methods on some datasets.

title: InstantSplat: Unbounded Sparse-view Pose-free Gaussian Splatting in 40 Seconds
summary: A self-supervised, pose-free sparse-view 3D reconstruction system that initializes dense pixel-aligned geometry from the MASt3R stereo prior, prunes redundant points via co-visibility checks, and jointly optimizes 3D Gaussians and camera poses through differentiable rasterization with a photometric loss (Gaussian Bundle Adjustment), reconstructing scenes in seconds instead of the COLMAP+3D-GS pipeline.

title: Visual Autoregressive Modeling: Scalable Image Generation via Next-Scale Prediction
summary: The paper proposes VAR, a visual generation paradigm that replaces raster-scan next-token prediction with coarse-to-fine next-scale prediction over multi-scale VQ token maps, using a GPT-2-style decoder-only transformer with AdaLN, achieving state-of-the-art ImageNet generation results, observed scaling laws, and zero-shot editing/inpainting generalization.

title: ReFT: Representation Finetuning for Language Models
summary: The paper proposes Representation Finetuning (ReFT): instead of updating weights of a frozen pretrained LM, it learns small interventions that edit hidden representations at chosen layers and token positions. LoReFT edits representations within a learned low-rank orthonormal subspace; DiReFT is a cheaper ablation without the orthogonality/difference terms. Reported results show 15x-65x fewer trained parameters than LoRA with competitive performan

title: LLM2Vec: Large Language Models Are Secretly Powerful Text Encoders
summary: A three-step unsupervised recipe (enable bidirectional attention, masked next-token prediction, SimCSE-style contrastive learning) that converts decoder-only LLMs into strong text encoders, achieving state-of-the-art unsupervised MTEB results.

title: RULER: What's the Real Context Size of Your Long-Context Language Models?
summary: RULER is a synthetic benchmark (not a model) for evaluating long-context LMs across four task categories — retrieval (NIAH variants), multi-hop tracing (variable tracking), aggregation (common/frequent word extraction), and question answering — with configurable sequence length and task complexity, showing that most models claiming 32K+ context degrade well before their claimed lengths.

title: InstantMesh: Efficient 3D Mesh Generation from a Single Image with Sparse-view Large Reconstruction Models
summary: A feed-forward image-to-3D pipeline combining a fine-tuned multi-view diffusion model (Zero123++) with a transformer-based sparse-view large reconstruction model (LRM-style) that predicts triplanes and extracts meshes via differentiable FlexiCubes iso-surface extraction, enabling direct depth/normal supervision and ~10 second mesh generation.

title: CyberSecEval 2: A Wide-Ranging Cybersecurity Evaluation Suite for Large Language Models
summary: The paper introduces CyberSecEval 2, a benchmark suite quantifying LLM cybersecurity risks and capabilities: new prompt-injection tests (15 techniques), code-interpreter abuse tests (5 categories, 500 prompts), vulnerability-exploitation capture-the-flag challenges, and a False Refusal Rate (FRR) dataset measuring the safety-utility tradeoff.
